# CellRune

> Rust XLSX/XLSM backend with deterministic, explicitly scoped formula
> calculation and a package-backed round-trip document foundation. Reading and
> calculation are separate operations, macros are never executed, external
> links are never followed, and parsing, calculation, and writing costs are
> bounded.

This file is a condensed, code-accurate reference for coding agents and other
tools that add `cellrune` as a dependency. It is hand-maintained against the
`pub use` list in `crates/cellrune/src/lib.rs`; treat a mismatch with that file
as a bug in this file, not in the crate. The version described by this file is
0.1.26, uses Semantic Versioning, and requires Rust 1.88 or newer. Runnable,
task-focused patterns are shipped as `examples/` in the crate package and live
at `crates/cellrune/examples/` in the repository workspace.

## Quick start

```rust
use cellrune::{
    CalculationCellResult, CalculationOptions, ReadOptions, calculate_workbook, read_xlsx_path,
};

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let workbook = read_xlsx_path("input.xlsx", ReadOptions::default())?;
    let calculation = calculate_workbook(&workbook, CalculationOptions::default());

    for (cell, result) in calculation.cells() {
        match result {
            CalculationCellResult::Value(value) => println!("{cell:?}: {value:?}"),
            CalculationCellResult::Unavailable(issue) => {
                eprintln!("{cell:?}: {}", issue.code().as_str());
            }
        }
    }

    Ok(())
}
```

Reading and calculation are separate calls. Reading alone never calculates a
formula; calculating never mutates the `WorkbookSnapshot` you read or the
XLSX file's own saved results. Calculation attempts every formula and returns
either a typed `CalculationCellResult::Value` or a structured
`CalculationCellResult::Unavailable` issue for each one. Independent formulas
still produce values when another formula is unavailable. Volatile functions
`TODAY()`, `NOW()`, `RAND()`, `RANDBETWEEN()`, and `RANDARRAY()` require
explicit deterministic inputs through `CalculationOptions`, or the formula
reports `VolatileInputMissing` instead of guessing.

For round-trip work, `open_xlsx_document_*` retains the exact input archive,
readable through `input_bytes()`, and binds it to a SHA-256 `InputHash`.
`open_xlsx_document_vec(Vec<u8>, OpenOptions)` keeps the caller's allocation as
that archive, and `XlsxDocument::into_input_bytes()` returns it.
`write_recalculated_xlsx_bytes`, `write_recalculated_xlsx`, and
`write_recalculated_xlsx_path` materialize a `CalculationSnapshot` made from
that exact document, preserve unrelated package content, and reopen the output
before success. A successful `WriteReport::output_hash()` is an `OutputHash`,
the SHA-256 identity of those exact verified output bytes; it is intentionally
not interchangeable with `InputHash`. The default strict policy produces no
artifact if any result is unavailable. `write_preserved_xlsx_bytes` produces
an unchanged preservation copy.

`WorkbookDraft::new()` creates a canonical XLSX workbook.
`WorkbookDraft::from_document(&XlsxDocument)` creates a preservation-backed edit
session. Effective calculation-semantic mutations advance the semantic
revision; presentation-only mutations use a separate revision, and accepted
no-ops keep the corresponding revision unchanged. Calculate `draft.workbook()`
after the final semantic edit, then call `write_xlsx_draft_bytes`,
`write_xlsx_draft`, or `write_xlsx_draft_path`. To write a document draft's
edits without calculating, call `write_xlsx_draft_edits_bytes`,
`write_xlsx_draft_edits`, or `write_xlsx_draft_edits_path`: affected formulas
lose their saved results and the host recalculates them on open.

`open_xlsx_document_*` also captures a separate `DocumentPresentation`.
It exposes shared/inline phonetic runs, explicit/effective phonetic visibility,
and default frozen panes without changing `CellValue::Text` or the calculation
fingerprint. `WorkbookDraft` provides atomic annotated-text and frozen-pane
mutations with a separate presentation revision. `PhoneticTextRange` uses
zero-based half-open UTF-16 code-unit offsets; when a range is applied to base
text, its boundaries are validated not to split a surrogate pair.
`CellPhonetics::resolved_runs` performs that translation into byte offsets, so
a consumer never writes its own UTF-16 conversion. See
`write_phonetic_workbook` and `inspect_phonetic_workbook` in the examples.

For AI hosts, the separate `cellrune-mcp` binary provides local stdio MCP
`2025-11-25` tools over `cellrune-interop::WorkbookSession`. It exposes
high-level workbook lifecycle, summary, range, usage, capability, batch edit, preview,
recalculation, delta, and Save As operations—not one tool per spreadsheet
function. Configured filesystem roots are canonicalized at startup; every
workbook path supplied to a tool must be absolute and contain no `..` component
(otherwise `mcp.path.absolute_required` or `mcp.path.invalid`), and must name a
location under a root as configured or as canonicalized, comparing components
exactly except that Windows ignores ASCII case; paths outside every root,
including UNC shares, device paths, and other spellings of a root such as
another symlink or junction to it or a Windows 8.3 short name, return
`mcp.path.outside_root` before any filesystem access. An input must then resolve
inside an allowed root and a Save As destination inside the root it names. It has no remote transport. The 25 tools are `workbook_create`,
`workbook_open`, `workbook_open_csv`, `workbook_close`, `workbook_summary`,
`workbook_export_csv`, `workbook_read_range`,
`workbook_read_formats`, `workbook_data_validations`, `workbook_hyperlinks`,
`workbook_comments`, `workbook_function_usage`, `workbook_scan_capabilities`,
`workbook_apply_changes`, `workbook_apply_changes_v2`, `workbook_recalculate`, `workbook_calculate_targets`,
`workbook_changes_since`, `workbook_save_as`, `workbook_save_edits_as`, `workbook_preview_changes`,
`workbook_preview_changes_page`, `workbook_commit_preview`,
`workbook_discard_preview`, and the sessionless `format_display_text`. `workbook_save_edits_as` is the edits-only write of
`write_xlsx_draft_edits_bytes` for a session opened from a file. MCP clients
always use the default read and calculation limits.
Read-only JSON resources expose the versioned function catalog at
`cellrune://support/functions` and active session metadata through the
`cellrune://sessions/{session_id}/summary` template. Operators can bound
resident sessions, idle lifetime, response bytes, and workbook bytes with
the corresponding `cellrune-mcp --help` options. Input validation and parsing
use the same capability-bound file handle and archive-byte ceiling. Preview
detail pages are byte-bounded and use opaque core cursors. At capacity,
create/open may evict the least-recently-used idle session; active sessions are
never evicted. Expiry or LRU eviction drops the interop session and therefore
discards its retained preview; MCP does not keep a second preview cache.

The Python `Workbook` is a context manager. Python and Node.js `Workbook`
objects also expose `closed` and an idempotent `close()`. Once `close()`
returns, the binding-owned native session has been released. An active
calculation is cooperatively cancelled and a published preview is discarded;
subsequent operations fail with the stable `interop.session.closed` code.

The binding preview calls are transport views of that single
interop-owned transaction. Python uses synchronous `Workbook.preview_changes`,
`preview_changes_page`, `commit_preview`, and `discard_preview`; the long
native preview operation releases the GIL. Python returns snake-case DTO fields
and ordinary integer IDs. Node uses Promise-backed
`await workbook.previewChanges(expectedRevision, changes, options)`, followed
by synchronous `previewChangesPage`, `commitPreview`, and `discardPreview`.
Node returns camel-case DTO fields and `bigint` IDs/cursors. A failed or
cancelled replacement preserves a previous published preview; pre-commit
cancellation or resource failure is retryable, while stale and successful
commits consume the preview.

Both bindings save in two ways. Python `save`/`to_bytes` and Node
`save`/`toBytes` write calculated results under the strict or invalidating
policy. Python `save_edits`/`edits_to_bytes` and Node `saveEdits`/`editsToBytes`
write only the edits of a workbook opened from a package, without calculating,
and return an edit report (`affected_formulas`/`affectedFormulas`,
`requests_host_recalculation`/`requestsHostRecalculation`, changed and removed
parts, input and output SHA-256). Node `save`, `toBytes`, `saveEdits`, and
`editsToBytes` read the workbook when their worker runs, not when called, so do
not edit it until the Promise settles: an edit made meanwhile may or may not be
saved, or may fail with `interop.session.unavailable`. Opening takes
`read_limits`/`readLimits`, and `calculate`, `recalculate`, and previews take
`calculation_limits`/`calculationLimits`: objects keyed by the Rust limit names
(snake case in Python, camel case in Node) whose omitted entries keep their
defaults. A zero fails with `interop.limit.invalid`; limits that are not an
object (a `dict` in Python), an unknown name, or a value that is not a positive
integer with `interop.limit.payload_invalid`. `scan_capabilities`/
`scanCapabilities` page through the static capability report. Range cells
carry `number_format` (`id`, `code`, `kind`); summaries carry each sheet's
`auto_filter` range, its `auto_filter_filtered_columns`, the `hidden_rows` as
A1 row ranges such as `2:4`, and `full_calculation_on_load`, which producers such as
xlsxwriter set while storing placeholder results. Python
`data_validations(sheet, offset=, limit=)` and Node.js
`dataValidations(sheet, { offset, limit })` page through a sheet's rules
(`WorkbookSession::data_validations(&SheetPageRequestDto)` in interop,
`workbook_data_validations` in MCP); each entry carries `ranges`,
`validation_type`, `operator`, and `error_style` OOXML tokens, `formula1`,
`formula2`, `allow_blank`, `in_cell_dropdown`, the two message flags, and the
error and prompt titles and messages. `hyperlinks(sheet, ...)` and
`comments(sheet, ...)` (interop `WorkbookSession::hyperlinks`/`comments`,
MCP `workbook_hyperlinks`/`workbook_comments`) page the same way through
`range`, `target`, `location`, `display`, `tooltip` and `address`, `author`,
`text` entries. Python `read_formats(sheet, start, end,
offset=, limit=)` and Node.js `readFormats(sheet, start, end, { offset, limit
})` (`WorkbookSession::read_formats(&RangeRequestDto) -> CellFormatPageDto`,
MCP `workbook_read_formats`) return each cell's `font`, `fill` (tagged
`pattern` or `gradient`), `border`, and `alignment`, with colors tagged
`argb`/`theme`/`indexed`/`automatic` plus `tint`, the range's
`column_widths`, and the page's `row_heights`. Edit schema v2 adds
`set_cell_format` (`sheet`, `address`, optional `font`, `fill` pattern,
`border`, `alignment`), `set_column_width` (`first`, `last`, `width` or
null), and `set_row_height` (`row`, `height` or null); Node uses the
camel-case kinds and fields. An
`xlsx.write.incomplete_calculation` error names the first 64 unavailable
formulas in `details.cells`. Python edits, setters, and `close()` release the
interpreter lock and wait for the session.

Sheets are deleted with the `delete_sheet` change (`{"kind": "delete_sheet",
"sheet": name}` in interop JSON, Python, and MCP; `{ kind: "deleteSheet",
sheet }` in Node) or the Python `delete_sheet(name)` and Node
`deleteSheet(name)` methods. Within a batch, later changes no longer reach a
deleted sheet by name. A delta, including one read later through
`changes_since`/`changesSince` or a committed preview's, names a deleted
sheet's removed results by the name the sheet had.

## Naming conventions

These patterns are consistent across the entire public API. When a function
or method isn't shown in an example below, generalize from these rules rather
than guessing a name from a different XLSX crate (`calamine`,
`rust_xlsxwriter`, `umya-spreadsheet`, etc.) — their shapes do not carry over.

- **Everything public is re-exported at the crate root.** Always
  `use cellrune::X`. Internal module paths such as `cellrune::xlsx::...` or
  `cellrune::calculation::...` are private implementation detail and are never
  part of the contract.
- **Validated newtypes are constructed through `::new(...)` or a named
  variant, returning `Result<Self, ValidationError>`.** There is no public way
  to violate the constructor contract documented by that type; a file-format
  boundary can impose additional rules without tightening an existing public
  constructor in a patch release. Examples: `Row::new(u32)`,
  `Column::new(u32)`, `SheetId::new(u32)`, `FiniteNumber::new(f64)`,
  `CellAddress::from_indices(row, column)`, `CellAddress::from_a1("A1")`,
  `SheetName::new(String)`, `TableName::new(String)`,
  `TableColumnName::new(String)`, `DiagnosticCode::new(String)`,
  `SourceId::new(String)`, `FormulaText::from_xlsx(String)` /
  `FormulaText::from_user_input(String)`, `DefinedName::new(...)`,
  `ProviderIdentity::new(name, version)`, `Diagnostic::new(...)`,
  `CellRange::new(start, end)`.
- **Limit construction is family-specific:** `ReadLimits`, `WriteLimits`, and
  `CalculationLimits` start from `Default::default()` and use
  `.with_max_x(value)`, returning `ReadOptionsError`, `WriteOptionsError`, or
  `CalculationOptionsError` when a zero budget is rejected. `SessionLimits`
  uses either `Default::default()` or the five-argument
  `SessionLimits::new(...) -> Result<Self, SessionError>`, then optionally
  `.with_formula_rewrite_limits(...)` and
  `.with_table_materialization_limit(...)`. Option constructors and
  non-budget setters such as
  `ReadOptions::new`, `WriteOptions::new`,
  `RecalculationWriteOptions::new`,
  `CalculationOptions::with_today_serial`,
  `CalculationOptions::with_now_serial`,
  `CalculationOptions::with_random_seed`,
  `CalculationOptions::with_locale_profile`, and
  `CalculationOptions::with_limits` return `Self` directly.
- **Getters are bare nouns, never `get_`-prefixed,** and are frequently
  `const fn` (`.code()`, `.severity()`, `.limits()`,
  `.max_dependency_edges()`, `.today_serial()`).
- **Public failure/value families are owned by different boundaries — never mixed:**
  see the Error taxonomy table below. Pick the family by *what layer failed*,
  not by guessing a generic `Error`/`Result` shape.
- **Respect `#[non_exhaustive]` on public enums.** Examples include `CellValue`,
  `ExcelError`, `ValidationError`, `CalculationIssueCode`, `WorkbookChange`,
  `TransactionDetailItem`, `XlsxDocumentKind`, and `RecalculationWritePolicy`.
  A `match` on any enum marked this way needs a wildcard arm even if every
  current variant is handled.
- **Every stable machine code exposes `.as_str()`,** returning `&str` or
  `&'static str` for programmatic comparison and logging
  (`XlsxErrorCode::as_str`, `DiagnosticCode::as_str`,
  `CalculationIssueCode::as_str`, `ExcelError::as_str`). Never branch on the
  human-readable `Display`/message string — only on `.code()`/`.as_str()`.
- **Sheet and defined-name lookups are case-insensitive** but preserve and
  return the original spelling (`WorkbookSnapshot::sheet_by_name`,
  `DefinedName::name`).
- **Table lookup uses OOXML `displayName`, not `name`.** `displayName` is the
  workbook-global formula/UI name; `name` is the worksheet-local programmatic
  object-model name. Both preserve spelling and compare case-insensitively.
- **`CellAddress::from_a1` / `Sheet::cell_by_a1` accept only an unqualified
  A1 address** (`"A1"`, `"XFD1048576"`) — no sheet prefix, no `$` anchors.
  Those belong to formula-reference syntax, which this workbook-lookup helper
  deliberately rejects.

## Public API surface

### Entry points — reading

- `read_xlsx_path(path: impl AsRef<Path>, options: ReadOptions) -> Result<WorkbookSnapshot, XlsxReadError>`
- `read_xlsx_bytes(bytes: &[u8], options: ReadOptions) -> Result<WorkbookSnapshot, XlsxReadError>`
- `read_xlsx<R: Read + Seek>(reader: R, options: ReadOptions) -> Result<WorkbookSnapshot, XlsxReadError>`
- `inspect_package<R: Read + Seek>(reader: R, options: ReadOptions) -> Result<PackageSummary, XlsxReadError>` —
  discovers ZIP/OOXML parts (workbook, worksheets, styles, shared strings,
  external links, macros) under the same resource budget as a full read,
  without interpreting workbook semantics.
- `open_xlsx_document_path`, `open_xlsx_document_bytes`,
  `open_xlsx_document<R: Read + Seek + Send + 'static>`, and
  `open_xlsx_document_vec(Vec<u8>, OpenOptions)` return an `XlsxDocument`
  under the `OpenOptions`/`ReadLimits` budget. The document retains no host
  path and exposes no ZIP or XML types. `open_xlsx_document_vec` keeps the
  given allocation as the retained archive after checking its length against
  `max_archive_bytes`; the other entry points hold one copy while opening.
- `ReadOptions::default()` / `ReadOptions::new(ReadLimits)`, `.limits()`
- `ReadLimits::default()` + 28 `.with_max_*(u64) -> Result<Self, ReadOptionsError>` budgets:
  archive bytes, ZIP entry count, per-entry/total uncompressed bytes,
  compression ratio, XML depth/attributes, sheet count, cells per
  sheet/total, shared string count/bytes/total bytes, total materialized cell
  text bytes, defined names,
  formula bytes per-cell/total, merged-range declarations, tables,
  table columns, table name bytes, per-table filter declarations, per-table
  filter/sort attribute text, plus phonetic runs, annotated references, and
  phonetic text bytes. Exceeding the merged-range or table budgets fails the
  read with the dedicated `XlsxErrorCode` variants `TooManyMergedRanges`,
  `TooManyTables`, `TooManyTableColumns`, `TableNameTooLarge`,
  `TooManyTableFilterItems`, or `TableFilterTextTooLarge`. The cell text budget
  (default 256 MiB) charges every shared-string reference, inline string, and
  cached text result a cell materializes and fails with `TotalCellTextTooLarge`
  (`xlsx.total_cell_text_too_large`). Cell text decodes OOXML `_xHHHH_` escapes,
  and writers escape XML-forbidden characters the same way.
- A cell typed `t="d"` holds an ISO 8601 date (`YYYY-MM-DD`), date-time
  (`YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm[:ss[.fff]]`), or time (`hh:mm[:ss[.fff]]`), optionally
  followed by `Z`, and reads as a serial number in the workbook's date system.
  Surrounding ASCII whitespace is ignored. As in Excel, `24:00[:00]` ends the
  day, `9999-12-31T24:00` reads as 0, 1900-02-29 exists, and a date before
  the date system's first day (1900-01-01 or 1904-01-01) reads as `#VALUE!`;
  any other value fails with `InvalidCellValue`. A cached formula result of that
  type reads the same way. Once a draft changes the date system, saving it writes
  each `t="d"` literal as the serial number the draft keeps, also when an edit
  such as a number format change left its value.
- A limit failure's `XlsxReadError::observed() -> Option<u64>` is the value
  that exceeded the limit named by its code, in that limit's unit: bytes, a
  count, a nesting depth, or the uncompressed-to-compressed ratio rounded up.
  Entry sizes and ratios checked before inflation use the sizes the ZIP
  central directory declares, and a shared-string `uniqueCount` is reported
  as declared. Reading stops at the first value past a limit, so a running
  total reports that value rather than the size of the whole input. It is
  `None` for other codes and for failures with no measurement: a zero-byte
  compressed entry, a nested phonetic run, or a buffer the host cannot
  reserve, which fails with `ArchiveTooLarge` or `EntryTooLarge`.
  `TooManyPhoneticRuns` covers two limits; `.phonetic_run_limit()` returns
  `PhoneticRunLimitKind::PerItem` or `Total` for a run-limit failure and
  `None` for a nested run. A package part is read into one buffer of its
  declared size, and inflating past that size fails with
  `DeclaredSizeMismatch`. An entry whose compressed size exceeds the archive
  length fails with `InvalidZip` while the package is indexed.

### Workbook model — read-only, format-neutral

- `WorkbookSnapshot`: `.sheets() -> &[Sheet]`, `.sheet_by_id(SheetId)`,
  `.sheet_by_name(&str)`, `.table(&str) -> Option<&Table>` (workbook-global
  `displayName`, case-insensitive), `.table_by_id(TableId)`,
  `.table_column_by_id(TableId, TableColumnId)`,
  `.table_column(TableId, &str)` (case-insensitive column name),
  `.containing_table(SheetId, CellAddress)` (unique containing table),
  `.defined_names()`, `.diagnostics()`, `.date_system()`,
  `.calculation_hints()`, `.source()`, `.provenance()`, and
  `.non_worksheet_tab_ids()` (chartsheet, dialogsheet, and macrosheet IDs,
  which added sheets never reuse), and `.highest_sheet_id() -> Option<SheetId>`
  (the highest ID the workbook has used, including sheets deleted in the
  same draft or session; an added sheet receives the next one, so within a
  draft or session a deleted sheet's ID is never reused. Opening a file
  computes it from the tabs the file declares, so after a save and reopen
  a deleted sheet's ID can be given to an added sheet).
- `Sheet`: `.id()`, `.name() -> &SheetName`, `.visibility()`,
  `.cell(CellAddress) -> Option<&Cell>`, `.cell_by_a1(&str)`,
  `.cells()` (row-major order), `.len()`, `.is_empty()`, `.used_range()`,
  `.merged_ranges() -> &[CellRange]` (sorted by top-left address),
  `.tables() -> &[Table]` (XLSX declaration order),
  `.auto_filter() -> Option<&SheetAutoFilter>` (the worksheet-level
  autoFilter outside tables: `.range()`, zero-based `.filter_column_ids()`,
  and `.filtered_column_ids()`, the filter columns that declare a
  `filters`, `customFilters`, `top10`, `dynamicFilter`, `colorFilter`, or
  `iconFilter` condition; the conditions and sort XML are preserved, not
  modeled), `.hidden_rows() -> &[Row]` (ascending rows whose `<row
  hidden>` is true, read without the `zeroHeight` default) with
  `.is_row_hidden(Row)`, and `.data_validations() -> &[DataValidation]`
  (worksheet order: `<dataValidations>`, then the Excel 2010
  `x14:dataValidations` extension). Excel stores the rows a filter hides as hidden rows,
  so a hidden row inside an autoFilter with a filter condition may be a
  filtered row. A document-backed write keeps hidden rows, and the written
  output is verified to read back the same hidden rows.
- `DataValidation` (read-only): `.ranges() -> &[CellRange]` (`sqref`
  order), `.validation_type() -> DataValidationType`
  (`AnyValue | Whole | Decimal | List | Date | Time | TextLength | Custom`),
  `.operator() -> DataValidationOperator` (`Between` when omitted),
  `.formula1()`/`.formula2() -> Option<&str>` (stored text without `=`),
  `.allow_blank()`, `.in_cell_dropdown()` (the inverse of OOXML
  `showDropDown`), `.show_input_message()`, `.show_error_message()`,
  `.error_style() -> DataValidationErrorStyle` (`Stop | Warning |
  Information`), `.error_title()`, `.error_message()`, `.prompt_title()`,
  and `.prompt_message()`. The three enums are `#[non_exhaustive]` and
  `.as_str()` returns the OOXML token. A rule with a malformed `sqref`, a
  repeated formula, or an unknown token is left unmodeled; its XML is
  preserved. A sheet rename rewrites rule formulas as the saved part does,
  and fails with `validation.formula_rewrite_parse_failed` when a rule
  formula naming the sheet does not parse. Rules are not part of the
  semantic fingerprint.
- `Sheet::hyperlinks() -> &[Hyperlink]` (worksheet order) and
  `Sheet::comments() -> &[Comment]` (comments-part order) are read-only.
  `Hyperlink`: `.range()`, `.target()` (external target from the worksheet
  relationship; `None` for an internal or unresolved one), `.location()`,
  `.display()`, `.tooltip()`. `Comment`: `.address()`, `.author()`,
  `.text()` (plain text of every run, phonetic runs excluded). Comments come
  from the legacy comments part, which Excel also writes for threaded
  comments. A malformed hyperlink `ref`, an unreadable worksheet relationship
  part, or an unreadable comments part leaves that metadata out without
  failing the read. A sheet rename rewrites internal hyperlink locations;
  an external hyperlink's location points into its target and is kept.
- `Table`: `.id() -> TableId` (OOXML-valid non-zero, workbook-global stable ID),
  `.name() -> &TableName` (worksheet-local programmatic name),
  `.display_name() -> &TableName` (workbook-global formula/UI name),
  `.range()`, `.table_type()`, `.header_row_count()`, `.totals_row_count()`,
  `.totals_row_shown()`, `.columns() -> &[TableColumn]`, `.auto_filter()`,
  `.sort_state()`, `.style_info()`, and `.has_opaque_metadata()`.
- `TableColumn`: `.id() -> u32` (the original scalar API),
  `.column_id() -> TableColumnId` (typed non-zero stable identity),
  `.name()`, `.totals_row_function() -> Option<TotalsRowFunction>`,
  `.totals_row_label()`, `.calculated_column_formula()`, and
  `.totals_row_formula()`.
- `TableName` validates a table's formula/UI identity; `TableColumnName`
  validates a rename target and rejects a leading or trailing ASCII space
  because OOXML normalization would change that identity.
- `TableType` (`Worksheet | Xml | QueryTable`) exposes `.as_str()`.
  `TableFormula` exposes validated storage-form `.text()` and `.is_array()`.
  `TableAutoFilter` exposes its effective `.range()`,
  `.declared_range() -> Option<CellRange>` (absent when `autoFilter@ref` was
  omitted and inherited from the table), typed `.filter_columns()`, and an
  optional nested `.sort_state()`. Each `TableFilterColumn` exposes its zero-based
  `.column_id()`, button flags, and optional `TableFilterCriteria`
  (`Values | Custom | Dynamic | Color | Icon | Top`). `TableSortState`
  exposes `.range()`, `.case_sensitive()`, `.column_sort()`,
  `.sort_method()`, and typed `.conditions()`.
  Calendar, grouping, comparison, dynamic-filter, icon-set, sort-by, and
  sort-method tokens are exposed as non-exhaustive enums. Dynamic filters
  retain numeric `val`/`maxVal` through validated `TableNumericValue` source
  spellings and ISO `valIso`/`maxValIso` through validated
  `TableDateTimeValue` spellings. Strict SpreadsheetML rejects `maxVal`;
  Transitional SpreadsheetML may retain both serial and ISO forms.
  `TableStyleInfo` exposes its optional name plus the four first/last-column
  and row/column-stripe flags.
- `TotalsRowFunction` (`#[non_exhaustive]`): `Sum | Min | Max | Average |
  Count | CountNumbers | StdDev | Var | Custom`; `.as_str()` returns the
  OOXML token. Invalid table definitions, duplicate IDs or display names,
  worksheet-local duplicate programmatic names, and defined-name conflicts
  are reported as `xlsx.table.*` warning diagnostics and drop only that
  table. A later table whose range overlaps an already accepted table is
  likewise dropped with `xlsx.table.overlap`; merged-range problems use
  `xlsx.merged_range.*`. Chartsheets, dialogsheets, and macrosheets are not
  calculation sheets: they are skipped with an `xlsx.sheet.non_worksheet`
  warning, keep their tab position on save, and count toward `SHEET`/`SHEETS`.
- `Cell`: `.address()`, `.content() -> &CellContent`, `.number_format()`.
- `CellContent::Literal(CellValue) | Formula(FormulaCell)`.
- `CellValue` (`#[non_exhaustive]`): `Blank | Number(FiniteNumber) | Text(String) | Logical(bool) | Error(ExcelError)`.
- `ExcelError` (`#[non_exhaustive]`): `#NULL!`, `#DIV/0!`, `#VALUE!`, `#REF!`,
  `#NAME?`, `#NUM!`, `#N/A`, `#GETTING_DATA`, `#SPILL!`, `#CALC!`, `#FIELD!`,
  `#BLOCKED!`, `#CONNECT!`, `#BUSY!`, `#UNKNOWN!`, and `#PYTHON!`. A formula
  that reads `#GETTING_DATA` or one of the last six reports an unsupported
  capability. A cell or row without the optional `r` follows the previous one;
  a shared formula's relative references wrap past the grid edge as Excel's
  copy does. A document open preserves a view or pane it cannot model with an
  `xlsx.pane.invalid` presentation diagnostic instead of failing.
- `CellAddress`: `::from_a1(&str)`, `::from_indices(row, column)`, `.row()`,
  `.column()`; `Display` renders `"A1"` style.
- `Row` / `Column`: 1-based, validated against `1..=1_048_576` /
  `1..=16_384` (`EXCEL_MAX_ROWS` / `EXCEL_MAX_COLUMNS`).
- `CellRange::new(start, end)`, `.start()`, `.end()`, `.height()`, `.width()`,
  `.contains(CellAddress)`.
- `FiniteNumber::new(f64)` — rejects NaN/±infinity; required wrapper for
  every numeric cell value and numeric option (e.g. `TODAY()`/`NOW()` serials).
- `SheetId`, `SheetName`, `SheetVisibility` (`Visible | Hidden | VeryHidden`),
  `DateSystem` (`Excel1900 | Excel1904`), `CalculationMode`,
  `CalculationHints`; calculation hints expose mode, calculation ID, host
  recalculation flags, and the optional iterative-calculation declaration.
  `CalculationHints::with_iterative_calculation(...)` sets that declaration.
  `WorkbookSource` / `WorkbookSourceKind`.
- `DefinedName`: `.name()`, `.scope()` (`DefinedNameScope::Workbook | Sheet(SheetId)`),
  `.formula() -> &FormulaText`, `.hidden()`.

### Defined-name inspection

- `analyze_defined_name(&WorkbookSnapshot, name, current_sheet)` uses default
  bounded options. `analyze_defined_name_with_options(...)` accepts
  `DefinedNameAnalysisOptions`, and `analyze_defined_name_cancellable(...)`
  additionally accepts a request-owned `CancellationToken`.
- `DefinedNameAnalysis` distinguishes `Rectangular`, `ThreeDimensional`,
  ordered `NonRectangular` areas, `EmptyReference`, `DynamicFormula`,
  `Constant`, typed `ExternalReference`, `Invalid`, `Unsupported`, and
  `NotFound`. Sheet spans and area order/multiplicity are preserved.
- `DefinedNameAnalysisOptions::new(CalculationOptions)` reuses formula,
  reference-area, and pairwise-work limits and adds configurable
  name-chain-depth and cumulative scan-node limits.
- Execution failures are separate from semantic results:
  `DefinedNameAnalysisError` reports `UnknownCurrentSheet`,
  `ResourceLimit`, or `Cancelled`, with a typed
  `DefinedNameAnalysisLimitKind` when a budget was exhausted.

### CSV

- `read_csv(&[u8], &CsvReadOptions) -> Result<WorkbookDraft, CsvError>`
  reads RFC 4180 UTF-8 (optional BOM; CRLF, LF, or CR records; `""` escapes)
  into a one-sheet draft. `CsvReadOptions::new()`, `.with_delimiter(char)`
  (one ASCII character other than a quote or line break),
  `.with_sheet_name(SheetName)` (default `Sheet1`), `.with_max_cells(u64)`
  (default `ReadLimits::max_cells_per_sheet`). Value rule: an empty unquoted
  field is no cell; a quoted field is text; an unquoted field is a number when
  it matches `[+-]?(d+[.d*]|.d+)([eE][+-]?d+)?`, a logical for `TRUE`/`FALSE`
  in any case, an error for an exact Excel error spelling, and text otherwise;
  no field is a formula and no date is parsed.
- `write_csv(&WorkbookSnapshot, &CalculationSnapshot, SheetId,
  CsvWriteOptions) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CsvError>` writes A1 through the last
  used cell, CRLF after every record, numbers as their shortest round-trip
  decimal, formulas and spilled cells as their calculated values, and quotes
  text that would read back as anything else.
- `CsvError::code() -> CsvErrorCode`: `csv.invalid_delimiter`,
  `csv.read.invalid_utf8`, `csv.read.unterminated_quote`,
  `csv.read.invalid_quote`, `csv.read.too_many_rows`,
  `csv.read.too_many_columns`, `csv.read.too_many_cells`,
  `csv.read.invalid_value`, `csv.write.unknown_sheet`,
  `csv.write.stale_calculation`, `csv.write.unavailable_result`; `.detail()`
  names the line or cell.
- Interop `WorkbookSession::open_csv_bytes(&[u8], &CsvReadOptionsDto)` and
  `save_csv_bytes(&CsvWriteRequestDto)` (requires a current calculation);
  Python `Workbook.from_csv(data, sheet_name=, delimiter=)`/`to_csv(sheet,
  delimiter=)`; Node.js `Workbook.fromCsv(bytes, { sheetName, delimiter })`
  (synchronous)/`toCsv(sheet, { delimiter })` returning a `Buffer`; MCP
  `workbook_open_csv` (path beneath a root) and `workbook_export_csv`
  (returns the text, bounded by the response limit).

### Package-backed document and preservation writing

- `XlsxDocument`: `.workbook()`, `.input_hash()`, `.input_bytes()`,
  `.into_input_bytes()`, `.kind()`, `.semantic_revision()`, `.presentation()`,
  `.presentation_revision()`, `.package_summary()`, `.workbook_part()`,
  `.worksheet_part(SheetId)`, and `.table_part(TableId)`. `.input_bytes() ->
  &[u8]` borrows the exact archive bytes retained for round-trip writing;
  `.input_hash()` is their SHA-256. `.into_input_bytes() -> Vec<u8>` consumes
  the document and returns those bytes without copying when it is their only
  owner; a clone or a draft made from it makes the call copy them.
- `XlsxDocumentKind`: `Xlsx | Xlsm`. Macro parts are retained but never
  executed.
- `write_preserved_xlsx_bytes(&XlsxDocument, WriteOptions) ->
  Result<Vec<u8>, XlsxWriteError>` raw-copies every unchanged ZIP entry.
- Accepted table metadata participates in write verification. Unchanged
  source-linked table parts are retained byte-for-byte. Stable-ID table
  authoring patches only modeled SpreadsheetML children and attributes in the
  accepted table part; foreign namespace and opaque extension content is
  preserved. The canonical serializer emits modeled worksheet tables and
  fails with `UnsupportedPreservation` rather than discard opaque metadata or
  invent the dependent parts required by query/XML tables, differential
  formats, or custom table styles. Canonical serialization also enforces the
  complete OOXML table-name and column-name rules even though the older public
  constructors retain their 0.1.8 validation contract for patch-version
  compatibility.
- `write_recalculated_xlsx_bytes(&XlsxDocument, &CalculationSnapshot,
  RecalculationWriteOptions) -> Result<RecalculatedWorkbook,
  XlsxWriteError>` prepares owned verified bytes plus a `WriteReport`.
- `write_recalculated_xlsx(&XlsxDocument, &CalculationSnapshot, &mut impl
  Write, RecalculationWriteOptions) -> Result<WriteReport, XlsxWriteError>`
  prepares and verifies all bytes before touching the writer.
- `write_recalculated_xlsx_path(...) -> Result<WriteReport,
  XlsxWriteError>` uses a sibling temporary file and refuses existing
  destinations unless `WriteOptions::with_replace_existing(true)` is set.
- `RecalculationWritePolicy`: `RequireComplete` (default) or
  `InvalidateUnavailable`. Invalidation removes stale caches, requests host
  recalculation, and records every affected cell and diagnostic.
- `WriteReport`: `.is_complete()`, `.policy()`, `.materialized_count()`,
  `.invalidated_cells()`, `.changed_parts()`, `.removed_parts()`,
  `.diagnostics()`, and `.provenance()`.
- `RecalculatedWorkbook`: `.bytes()`, `.into_bytes()`, `.report()`,
  `.into_parts()`, and `.save_path(...)`.
- With the optional `capability-fs` feature,
  `RecalculatedWorkbook::save_in_directory(&cap_std::fs::Dir, file_name,
  WriteOptions)` installs beneath an already-open directory identity. The
  destination must be one relative file name; this is the primitive used by
  the MCP Save As boundary.
- `WriteOptions::default()` refuses implicit destination replacement.
  `WriteLimits` owns output, entry, XML, edit, result, relationship, temporary
  storage, and verification budgets.
- Branch on `XlsxWriteError::code()` /
  `XlsxWriteErrorCode::as_str()`, never on human-readable messages.

### Workbook authoring and typed edits

- `WorkbookDraft::new()` starts with visible `Sheet1`;
  `WorkbookDraft::from_document(&XlsxDocument)` retains the exact source
  package privately.
- `.workbook()`, `.presentation()`, `.semantic_revision()`,
  `.presentation_revision()`, `.is_document_backed()`.
- `.set_cell_value(...)`, `.set_cell_formula(...)`,
  `.set_cell_dynamic_formula(..., Option<CellRange>)`, `.clear_cell(...)`,
  `.set_cell_number_format(...)`.
- `.set_annotated_text(...)`, `.set_phonetics(...)`, `.clear_phonetics(...)`,
  `.set_frozen_pane(...)`, `.clear_frozen_pane(...)`.
- `.add_sheet(...)`, `.rename_sheet(...)`, `.delete_sheet(SheetId)`,
  `.move_sheet(SheetId, position)`, `.set_sheet_visibility(...)`.
- `.set_defined_name(...)`, `.remove_defined_name(...)`,
  `.set_date_system(...)`, `.set_calculation_hints(...)`.
- `NumberFormat::built_in(...)` and `NumberFormat::custom(...)` validate the
  built-in/custom ID boundary. `NumberFormatKind` distinguishes general,
  numeric, date, time, date-time, and duration interpretation. Custom formats
  require a nonempty code.
- `write_xlsx_draft_bytes`, `write_xlsx_draft`, and
  `write_xlsx_draft_path` require a `CalculationSnapshot` produced from the
  current `draft.workbook()`. New drafts produce deterministic canonical
  XLSX; document drafts preserve unrelated XLSX/XLSM parts.
- `write_xlsx_draft_edits_bytes(&WorkbookDraft, WriteOptions) ->
  Result<EditedWorkbook, XlsxWriteError>`, `write_xlsx_draft_edits(&draft,
  &mut impl Write, WriteOptions)`, and `write_xlsx_draft_edits_path(&draft,
  path, WriteOptions) -> Result<EditWriteReport, XlsxWriteError>` write a
  document draft's edits without calculating; a new draft fails with
  `InvalidPackagePlan`. A static analysis of the edited workbook finds the
  formulas the edits can affect: edited formulas; formulas referring to
  edited or removed cells, including through ranges, whole columns or rows,
  and the full reach of an `INDEX` range end; formulas naming a changed
  defined name, directly, through other names, through a sheet-qualified
  name such as `Data!Rate`, or while it did not exist; formulas referring to
  a changed table; references to an added, renamed, or deleted sheet, and
  `SHEET`, `SHEETS`, `CELL`, and 3-D references when sheets are added,
  renamed, or deleted; a
  spill anchor whose area was written; anchors with a saved `#SPILL!` after
  a clear; and every dependent of those. An `OFFSET` whose position the
  edited workbook gives without calculating anything counts as reading the
  cells it resolves to. Formulas whose references are known only after
  evaluation (`INDIRECT`, any other `OFFSET`, a range end computed from
  values, unparsed formulas, rejected calls, also inside a defined name they
  use, formulas without text) are always affected once anything changed,
  and every formula is affected when
  the analysis exceeds `max_dependency_edges` or the date system or
  calculation hints changed. Affected formulas lose their saved
  results and only then does `calcPr` gain `fullCalcOnLoad="1"`, keeping
  `forceFullCalc`; other saved results, `calcPr`, `calcChain.xml` while every
  formula keeps its cell and array kind, and untouched parts keep their
  bytes. The output is verified before success.
- `EditWriteReport`: `.affected_formulas()` (cell order),
  `.requests_host_recalculation()`, `.changed_parts()`, `.removed_parts()`
  (for example a `calcChain.xml` the edits invalidated), `.output_hash()`,
  `.input_hash()`, `.semantic_revision()`, `.presentation_revision()`.
  `EditedWorkbook`: `.bytes()`, `.into_bytes()`, `.report()`,
  `.into_parts()`, `.save_path(...)`, and with `capability-fs`
  `.save_in_directory(...)`.
- A cell a document draft creates takes its row's style when the row has
  `customFormat="1"`, else its column's `<col style>`, else none; an empty
  styled `<c>` keeps its own style unless it names no `cellXfs` entry.
  Writing text to a table header cell, also with `.set_annotated_text`,
  renames the column; edits inside a legacy array other than at its anchor
  fail with `validation.array_formula_part_edit`.
- Saving a document draft with deleted sheets drops each one's `<sheet>`
  entry, workbook relationship, and every part only deleted sheets reached,
  found through the package relationships: tables, drawings, charts,
  comments, pivot tables, and a pivot cache all of whose pivot tables went,
  with its `<pivotCache>` entry. A part another sheet still reaches stays,
  removed parts lose their content-type overrides, and `docProps/app.xml`
  keeps its bytes. Sheet-scoped names get renumbered `localSheetId`s, and
  `workbookView` `activeTab` and `firstSheet` count down by the deleted tabs
  before them. A deleted first tab hands its role to the tab now at its
  place; a deleted active tab hands activity to the nearest visible tab
  after it, else the nearest visible tab before it, as Excel does, and an
  `activeTab` of 0 is omitted; `tabSelected` is left as it was.
  Conditional formats, data validations, x14 formulas, and chart series that
  name a deleted sheet become `#REF!`; a sparkline whose data names one loses
  its data source and keeps its location, and an internal hyperlink keeps its
  location, as Excel saves them. A remaining pivot cache whose source is a
  deleted sheet or a table on one, a remaining pivot chart of a pivot table
  on one, a form control (`fmlaLink`, `fmlaRange`, `fmlaTxbx`, `fmlaGroup`),
  VML control (`x:FmlaLink`, `x:FmlaRange`), linked shape (`textlink`), or
  data consolidation (`dataRef sheet`) that names a deleted sheet, and any
  slicer or timeline cache while a deleted sheet holds a pivot table or
  table fail with `UnsupportedPreservation`, the detail naming the parts.
- Dynamic formulas can be authored in canonical drafts. Existing
  document-backed dynamic formulas can be recalculated and cache-rewritten,
  but adding or replacing one through a document draft fails with
  `UnsupportedPreservation` until source metadata-index merging is available.

### XLSX presentation

- `DocumentPresentation`: `.revision()`, `.diagnostics()`,
  `.frozen_pane(SheetId)`, `.worksheet_phonetic_properties(SheetId)`,
  `.row_phonetic_visibility(SheetId, Row)`,
  `.column_phonetic_visibility(SheetId)`,
  `.cell_phonetics(SheetId, CellAddress)`, and
  `.phonetic_cell_entries(SheetId) -> impl Iterator<Item = (CellAddress, CellPhonetics)>`.
  The iterator yields only cells carrying at least one run, in row-major
  address order, reporting the same visibility `cell_phonetics` reports for the
  same address. A cell whose annotation holds only `phoneticPr` display
  properties without `rPh` runs — common in Japanese workbooks — is skipped by
  the iterator and stays reachable through `cell_phonetics`.
- `CellPhonetics`: `.runs()`, `.properties()`,
  `.explicit_cell_visibility()`, `.explicit_row_visibility()`,
  `.explicit_column_visibility()`, `.effective_visibility()`, and
  `.resolved_runs(&str) -> Result<Vec<ResolvedPhoneticRun>, ValidationError>`.
- `ResolvedPhoneticRun`: `.base_bytes() -> Range<usize>`, `.base_slice()`,
  `.text()`, `.run()`. `resolved_runs` translates each run's range from the
  UTF-16 code units XLSX stores into the byte offsets Rust indexes with, and
  rejects a range that splits a surrogate pair or runs past the base text with
  the existing `ValidationError`. Presentation state does not hold cell text,
  so the base text comes from the workbook snapshot: look the address up with
  `WorkbookSnapshot::sheet_by_id(..).cell(address)` and match
  `CellContent::Literal(CellValue::Text(..))`. The returned value keeps that
  exact borrow, so a byte range cannot be paired with another cell's string.
- `PhoneticTextRange::new(start_utf16, end_utf16)`, `.start_utf16()`,
  `.end_utf16()`; when a range is validated against its base text, a boundary
  cannot split a surrogate pair.
- `PhoneticRun::new(range, text)`, `.base_range()`, `.text()`.
- `PhoneticProperties::new(font_id)`, `.font_id()`,
  `.effective_font_id()`, `.phonetic_type()`, `.alignment()`,
  `.with_phonetic_type(...)`, `.with_alignment(...)`.
- `PhoneticType`: `FullWidthKatakana | HalfWidthKatakana | Hiragana |
  NoConversion`; `PhoneticAlignment`: `NoControl | Left | Center |
  Distributed`.
- `ColumnPhoneticVisibility` records one column range and whether phonetics
  are shown for it.
- `PhoneticWriteOptions::show()` / `hide()` / `new(bool)`,
  `.with_properties(...)`.
- `FrozenPane::new(frozen_rows, frozen_columns)`, `.frozen_rows()`,
  `.frozen_columns()`, `.is_clear()`.
- Cell formats: `WorkbookDraft::cell_format(SheetId, CellAddress) ->
  Result<CellFormat, ValidationError>` resolves the edited format, else a
  kept valued source cell's own style, else the style a new cell takes there
  (blank cell, `customFormat` row, then column), else the default style;
  `WorkbookDraft::new()` defaults to Calibri 11. `CellFormat`: `.font() ->
  &Font` (`.name()`, `.size()`, `.bold()`, `.italic()`, `.underline() ->
  FontUnderline`, `.strike()`, `.color()`), `.fill() -> Fill`
  (`Pattern(PatternFill)` with `.pattern() -> FillPattern`,
  `.foreground()`, `.background()`, or `Gradient`, whose stops are not
  modeled), `.border() -> Border` (`.left()`, `.right()`, `.top()`,
  `.bottom()`, `.diagonal()` as `BorderEdge { .style() -> BorderStyle,
  .color() }`, `.diagonal_up()`, `.diagonal_down()`), and `.alignment() ->
  Alignment` (`HorizontalAlignment`, `VerticalAlignment`, `.wrap_text()`,
  `.shrink_to_fit()`, `.indent()` 0-250, `.text_rotation()` 0-180 or 255).
  `Color::argb(0xAARRGGBB)`, `::theme(i)`, `::indexed(i)`, `::automatic()`,
  `.with_tint(-1.0..=1.0)`, `.kind() -> ColorKind`, `.tint()`. Builders
  validate: `Font::with_name` (1-31 UTF-16 units, no control characters,
  else `FontNameInvalid`), `Font::with_size` (1-409 points), tints, indents,
  and rotations fail with `FormatValueOutOfRange { property, value }`. Token
  enums are `#[non_exhaustive]` with OOXML `.as_str()`/`::from_token`.
- Layout: `DocumentPresentation::column_widths(SheetId) -> &[ColumnWidth]`
  (`.first()`, `.last()`, `.width()` in characters; sorted,
  non-overlapping), `.column_width(SheetId, Column)`, `.row_heights(SheetId)`
  iterating `(Row, f64)` points, and `.row_height(SheetId, Row)`. Document
  opens capture source formats and layout; `read_xlsx_*` snapshots do not.
- Canonical authoring supports default font record `0`; source rich-text
  phonetic edits and right-to-left frozen-pane edits fail closed with
  `UnsupportedPreservation`.

### Atomic batches and persistent recalculation sessions

- `WorkbookChange` is the non-exhaustive typed mutation union. Construct
  changes with `set_cell_value`, `set_cell_formula`,
  `set_cell_dynamic_formula`, `clear_cell`, `set_cell_number_format`,
  `add_sheet`, `rename_sheet`, `delete_sheet`,
  `move_sheet(SheetId, position)`, `set_sheet_visibility`,
  `set_defined_name`,
  `remove_defined_name`, `rename_defined_name(scope, name, new_name)`,
  `set_date_system`, `set_calculation_hints`,
  `rename_table(TableId, TableName)`,
  `rename_table_column(TableId, TableColumnId, TableColumnName)`,
  `resize_table_rows(TableId, first_data_row, last_data_row)`,
  `widen_table_columns(TableId, CellRange)`, and
  `widen_sheet_auto_filter(SheetId, CellRange)`. A widening keeps the row
  span, contains the old range, keeps filter and sort state, shifts filter
  column IDs when it grows leftward, names new table columns from their text
  header cells, and moves `_xlnm._FilterDatabase` with a sheet filter.
  `set_cell_format(SheetId, CellAddress, CellFormatEdit)` (`.with_font`,
  `.with_fill(PatternFill)`, `.with_border`, `.with_alignment`; unset
  components keep their value), `set_column_width(SheetId, first: Column,
  last: Column, Option<f64>)` (0-255 characters), and
  `set_row_height(SheetId, Row, Option<f64>)` (0-409 points; `None`
  restores the default) are presentation changes: they advance only the
  presentation revision. A session install of a batch prepared before
  another presentation-only install fails with `RevisionMismatch`.
- `EditBatch::new(changes)` preserves operation order.
  `WorkbookDraft::apply_changes(batch)` stages once and commits one semantic
  revision or rolls the complete batch back. If every accepted operation is
  a semantic no-op, the receipt keeps the base revision and reports no
  topology or calculation-metadata change.
- Table and column renames rewrite every typed reference in worksheet cells,
  defined names, calculated-column formulas, and totals-row formulas while
  preserving source text outside the target spans. A table-qualified
  one-column reference to a renamed column is written as Excel saves it,
  `Orders[unit_price]`; in a selector list the name is bracketed,
  `Orders[[#Data],[unit_price]]`. Row resize keeps stable table/column
  identities, remaps filter/sort ranges, materializes modeled
  calculated/totals/header cells, and can expand a header-only empty table.
  Unsupported metadata, collisions, formula rewrite failures, limits, and
  cancellation roll back the complete batch.
- `delete_sheet(SheetId)` removes the sheet, the names scoped to it, and its
  tables, and rewrites the remaining cell formulas, defined names, and table
  formulas as Excel saves them: a reference or qualified name on the deleted
  sheet, a structured reference to one of its tables, and a range or spill
  reference with such an operand become `#REF!` (`SUM('S2'!A1:A3)` becomes
  `SUM(#REF!)`, and `'S2'!Name` becomes `#REF!` where Excel writes
  `[0]!Name`); a deleted end of a 3-D reference moves to the nearest
  remaining worksheet toward the other end, passing over chartsheets and
  other tabs that are not worksheets as Excel does, and an end left alone
  collapses (`'S2:S3'!A1` becomes `'S3'!A1`), while a
  deleted middle sheet leaves the text as it is. `INDIRECT` text and
  external references are untouched. Data validation formulas on other
  sheets that name the deleted sheet become `#REF!` in the model, as in the
  saved part, while hyperlink locations stay. Later tabs move forward, the
  draft drops what it recorded for the sheet (cells, tables, data
  validations, hyperlinks, comments, panes, cell formats, column widths,
  and row heights), and the receipt reports a topology
  change, so a session rebuilds and recalculates fully. Deleting the last
  visible sheet fails with `ValidationError::LastVisibleSheet`
  (`validation.last_visible_sheet`), an unknown sheet with `UnknownSheetId`.
- `move_sheet(SheetId, position)` moves a tab, a worksheet or a chartsheet,
  to zero-based `position` of the tab order counted after the move. The tab
  keeps its sheet ID and scoped names, which take its new `localSheetId`,
  and stays the active sheet if it was. A 3-D reference's tabs follow tab
  order, so it gains or loses the tabs moved across its ends and keeps its
  text, unless the move puts its ends out of order: the moved end then
  becomes its neighbour inside the old span, the start the next worksheet
  and the end the previous one, and ends that meet collapse, as Excel saves
  them (with tabs S1 to S6, moving S2 after S5 turns `'S2:S5'!A1` into
  `'S3:S5'!A1` and `'S2:S3'!A1` into `'S3'!A1`). Names follow the same rule;
  other references keep their text. A position past the last tab fails
  with `validation.sheet_position_out_of_range`, an unknown tab with
  `UnknownSheetId`; a move to the tab's own position is a no-op. The
  receipt reports a topology change. Saving into the source package writes
  the `<sheet>` entries in the new order, renumbers `localSheetId`, points
  `workbookView` `activeTab` and `firstSheet` at the same tabs, replays the
  draft's deletions and moves on 3-D references in preserved parts, and an
  edit-only save clears the results of 3-D references and sheet functions.
- `rename_defined_name(DefinedNameScope, name, new_name)` renames a defined
  name and rewrites the uses that resolve to it, as Excel does, in cell
  formulas, defined names, table formulas, and data validations, and on
  save in preserved conditional formats, data validations, x14 formulas,
  and chart series (`[0]!Name` included). A use resolves to a sheet's own
  name on that sheet or qualified with it (`'S2'!Rate`), else to the
  workbook name, so a workbook rename leaves uses of a sheet's own name as
  they are and a sheet rename rewrites only that sheet's and its qualified
  uses; a LAMBDA name is renamed where it is called, `INDIRECT` text and
  other workbooks' names stay. An unknown name fails with
  `validation.unknown_defined_name`, a collision in the same scope with
  `DuplicateDefinedName`, and a new name the other scope already uses,
  which would take over uses, with `validation.defined_name_rename_shadowed`.
  The receipt reports a topology change.
- `WorkbookCalculationSession::new(draft)` / `::create()` owns the mutable
  draft plus persistent parsed formulas, dependency state, results, dirty
  roots, and bounded delta history.
- `session.apply_changes(expected_revision, batch)` returns `EditReceipt`;
  it distinguishes all source/format changes from calculation-semantic
  changes, reports stable `.changed_table_ids()`, and records
  topology/metadata impact. Stale writers fail with
  `SessionErrorCode::RevisionMismatch`.
- To validate and size an edit before committing it, call
  `session.prepare_changes(expected_revision, batch)`. The returned
  `PreparedEditBatch` exposes the prospective `.workbook()` and `.receipt()`;
  `session.install_changes(prepared)` commits only if its base revision is
  still current. `prepare_changes_cancellable` adds cooperative cancellation
  to formula rewriting, table materialization, and final snapshot/index
  construction.
- `session.recalculate(RecalculationMode::Auto, options, token)` returns a
  `CalculationDelta`. `Auto` uses a proven dirty subset and falls back to
  full calculation for name/sheet/table/options or uncertain dynamic/spill
  topology. After edits that only add, replace, or remove cell formulas,
  `Auto` parses just those formulas, updates the dependency graph in place,
  and evaluates them and their dependents (`DirtySubset`, with the parsed
  count in `.parsed_formula_count()`); it compiles the workbook again
  (`TopologyChanged`) when an edited cell is or was part of an array
  formula, an edit adds a reference incremental calculation cannot follow,
  or the graph could reach `max_dependency_edges`, and reports
  `DynamicTopology` when the workbook already held such a reference.
  Forced `Incremental` fails closed when
  unsafe, including after formula edits. When the only
  options that differ from the installed calculation are the `TODAY()` serial,
  the `NOW()` serial, or the random seed, the dirty subset is the formulas
  calling a function that reads a changed input, directly or through defined
  names and `LAMBDA`, plus their dependents: `Auto` reports `DirtySubset`,
  `NoDirtyFormulas` when no formula reads the input, or a full
  `DynamicTopology` pass under uncertain dynamic topology, and forced
  `Incremental` proceeds. Any other option or limit change stays full.
- For work outside a session lock, call `prepare_recalculation`, run the
  returned `PreparedCalculation`, then call `install`. `CancellationToken`
  provides cooperative cancellation. Running a prepared calculation returns
  `CompletedCalculation`; cancellation or a newer workbook revision never
  replaces the installed current result.
- `session.prepare_transaction(expected_revision, batch, mode, options, token)`
  captures immutable base and candidate drafts without mutating the live
  session. Run its `PreparedWorkbookTransaction` off-lock to obtain a
  `CompletedWorkbookTransaction`. Its `.report()` is a complete transaction
  summary and `.page_from_token(section, cursor, limit)` consumes only its
  opaque core cursor contract. `validate_transaction` rejects a changed live
  basis before publication; `install_transaction_cancellable` atomically
  installs the exact candidate, receipt, and delta. Pre-commit cancellation or
  resource failure is retryable; stale and successful installation are terminal.
  `CompletedWorkbookTransaction::discard()` releases a candidate without
  changing the live session.
- `CalculationDelta` distinguishes dirty, evaluated, changed, and removed
  materialized cells. `CalculationDeltaCell` carries each changed cell,
  materialization origin, and result. `CalculationExecutionMode` reports
  `Incremental | Full`, while non-exhaustive `CalculationDecisionReason`
  explains why that schedule was selected. `changes_since(cursor, limit)`
  returns a bounded `CalculationDeltaPage`.
- `SessionLimits` bounds batch operations, evaluated formulas, delta cells,
  retained deltas, page size, cumulative formula-rewrite formula/source/AST/
  source-edit work, and table-resize materialized cells. `SessionErrorCode`
  is the stable machine-readable error family.
- `ApplyChangesError` distinguishes a staged `ValidationError` from a
  `SessionError`. `SessionError` exposes `.code()`, `.message()`, and
  `.detail()`.

### Formula storage — independent of calculation

- `FormulaCell`: `.dialect()`, `.text() -> Option<&FormulaText>`,
  `.saved_result() -> &SavedResult`, `.metadata() -> &FormulaMetadata`,
  `.recalculate_always()`.
- `FormulaText::from_xlsx(String)` keeps storage text verbatim;
  `::from_user_input(String)` removes the leading `=` and adds Excel's
  storage prefixes (`_xlfn.`, `_xlfn._xlws.` for `FILTER`/`SORT`, `_xlpm.` for
  `LET`/`LAMBDA` parameters, `_xleta.` for functions passed as `LAMBDA`
  arguments, `_xlfn.ANCHORARRAY` for `#`, `_xlfn.SINGLE` for `@`) without
  reprinting anything else; `.as_str()` returns that storage text.
- `SavedResult`: `Missing | Present(CellValue) | Invalid(SavedResultIssue)` —
  the value the *file itself* cached. `calculate_workbook` never reads or
  writes this; it is a separate, independent fact about the source.
- `FormulaMetadata` (`#[non_exhaustive]`): `Normal | Shared{..} | Array{..} | DynamicArray{..} | DataTable{..}`.
- `SharedFormulaRole`: `Anchor | Follower { anchor }`.
- `FormulaDialect` (`#[non_exhaustive]`): currently only `ExcelA1`.

### Capability inventory — optional

- `scan_formula_capabilities(&WorkbookSnapshot) -> FormulaCapabilityReport`
- `scan_formula_capabilities_with_options(&WorkbookSnapshot, CalculationOptions) -> FormulaCapabilityReport` —
  use this (with the same `CalculationLimits` you'll pass to
  `calculate_workbook`) to align static parse, name, and dependency budgets.
  Evaluation-only limits such as materialized array cells, calculated text
  bytes, and data-dependent iterations can still surface during calculation.
- `FormulaCapabilityReport`: `.entries()`, `.formula_count()`,
  `.supported_count()`, `.unsupported_count()`, `.is_supported()`.
- `FormulaCapabilityEntry`: `.cell()` and `.capability()`.
- `FormulaCapability`: `Supported | Unsupported(Vec<CalculationIssue>)`.
- The inventory is static: it does not calculate values, inspect saved values,
  or change what `calculate_workbook` returns. Use it for bulk migration
  planning, support dashboards, or user interfaces that need a formula-surface
  inventory. Normal workbook calculation does not require it.

### Function catalog and workbook demand

- `supported_function_catalog() -> Vec<FunctionCatalogEntry>` returns the
  deterministic accepted-name catalog for this build. Each entry exposes
  `.name()`, `.canonical_name()`, `.is_alias()`, `.returns_array()`, and
  `.is_official()`. The 0.1.27 catalog contains 495 official
  Excel-facing names and one non-official compatibility entry for the OOXML
  dummy-function marker, for 496 accepted entries. The descriptor registry
  retains versioned semantic snapshots, while the current catalog is guarded
  by structural and behavioral assertions rather than byte hashes. The 0.1.14
  catalog contained 386 official names and 387 accepted entries.
- The official names added in 0.1.27 are `SKEW`, `SKEW.P`, `KURT`,
  `FREQUENCY`, `MODE.MULT`, `CHISQ.TEST`, `CHITEST`, `CHISQ.INV`,
  `CHISQ.INV.RT`, `CHIINV`, `CUMIPMT`, `CUMPRINC`, `VDB`, `AMORLINC`,
  `AMORDEGRC`, `IMSIN`, `IMCOS`,
  `IMTAN`, `IMCOT`, `IMSEC`, `IMCSC`, `IMSINH`, `IMSECH`, `IMCSCH`,
  `ENCODEURL`, `BAHTTEXT`, and `CELL`. `CHITEST` and `CHIINV` are legacy
  aliases of
  `CHISQ.TEST` and `CHISQ.INV.RT`. `FREQUENCY` and `MODE.MULT` are marked
  `.returns_array()`; the others return scalars.
- `SKEW`, `SKEW.P`, and `KURT` collect numbers as `STDEV.S` does: typed text
  numbers and logical values
  count, while text, logical values, and blanks inside references and arrays
  are skipped, and errors propagate. `SKEW` and `KURT` standardize by the sample
  standard deviation and apply Microsoft's bias corrections; `SKEW.P` divides
  the summed cubed population z-scores by the count. Fewer than three numbers
  (four for `KURT`) or a zero standard deviation returns `#DIV/0!`.
- `FREQUENCY(data_array, bins_array)` spills one column with one more row than
  there are bins: the count of numbers at or below the first bin, above each
  bin through the next, and above the last bin. Text and blanks are ignored in
  both arguments, and bins without any number return the count of numbers.
  Bins must be in ascending order (repeats are empty intervals) and be all
  numbers or none; other bins, and logical values or errors in either
  argument, report `calculation.unsupported_expression`.
- `MODE.MULT` spills one column of every number that occurs most often, at
  least twice, in the order each first occurs, so its first row is the
  `MODE.SNGL` result; it collects numbers as `MODE.SNGL` does and returns
  `#N/A` when no number repeats.
- `CHISQ.INV(probability, deg_freedom)` and `CHISQ.INV.RT` invert the left and
  right tails of the chi-square distribution. They accept probabilities from 0
  through 1 and truncate the degrees of freedom to 1 through 10^10, otherwise
  `#NUM!`. A zero left tail or a full right tail is 0, the infinite quantile
  (left tail 1, right tail 0) is `#NUM!`, and a search that does not converge
  is `#N/A`. The right tail is solved directly, so tiny tails keep their
  relative precision.
- `CHISQ.TEST(actual_range, expected_range)` returns the right-tail probability
  of Σ (A − E)² / E with (r − 1)(c − 1) degrees of freedom, or one less than
  the length of a single row or column. Ranges with different numbers of values
  or a single value return `#N/A`. Equal counts in different shapes, values
  that are not numbers, and expected values that are not positive report
  `calculation.unsupported_expression`.
- `CUMIPMT` and `CUMPRINC(rate, nper, pv, start_period, end_period, type)`
  total the interest or principal of the level payments from `start_period`
  through `end_period` as negative amounts. A rate, `nper`, or `pv` that is
  not positive, a start or end period below 1, a start after the end, an end
  after `nper`, or a type other than 0 or 1 returns `#NUM!`. Fractional periods
  and beginning-of-period payments (type 1) report
  `calculation.unsupported_expression`.
- `VDB(cost, salvage, life, start_period, end_period, [factor], [no_switch])`
  totals the declining-balance depreciation (factor 2 when absent) of the
  periods after `start_period` through `end_period`, never below salvage, and
  unless `no_switch` is TRUE spreads the remaining depreciable amount evenly
  over the remaining life from the first period in which that exceeds the
  declining balance. Salvage above cost depreciates nothing. A negative cost,
  salvage, or start, a life or factor that is not positive, or an end before the
  start returns `#NUM!`; fractional periods and an end after the life report
  `calculation.unsupported_expression`.
- `AMORLINC` and `AMORDEGRC(cost, date_purchased, first_period, salvage,
  period, rate, [basis])` prorate period 0 by the `YEARFRAC` fraction from the
  purchase date to the end of the first period in basis 0 (absent), 1, 3, or 4.
  `AMORLINC` then depreciates cost × rate per period and the remainder down to
  salvage in the following period, then 0. `AMORDEGRC` multiplies the rate by
  1.5 for a life (1/rate) from 3 through 4 years, 2 from 5 through 6, and 2.5
  above 6, depreciates the book value at that rate each period, and rounds
  each amount to a whole number; a life strictly between 0 and 3 other than 1
  and 2, or strictly between 4 and 5, returns `#NUM!`. A salvage above the cost
  returns `#NUM!`. Other invalid arguments, another basis, a fractional period,
  a purchase after the first period, `AMORDEGRC` periods within two of the end
  of the life or past salvage, a life of exactly 1 or 2, a rounding tie, and an
  `AMORLINC` first period above the depreciable amount report
  `calculation.unsupported_expression`.
- The complex trigonometric functions take one inumber and return complex text
  with the same 15-significant-digit formatting and `i`/`j` suffix as the other
  complex functions; `IMTAN` and `IMCOT` use the double-angle forms so small
  real parts survive. A logical inumber returns `#VALUE!` and other text that
  is not a complex number `#NUM!`. `IMSIN`, `IMCOS`, and `IMSINH` return
  `#NUM!` when the result overflows. `IMCOT`, `IMCSC`, and `IMCSCH` at zero, and
  the bounded functions where an intermediate overflows, report
  `calculation.unsupported_expression`.
- `ENCODEURL(text)` percent-encodes the text as RFC 3986 encodes a URI
  component: ASCII letters, digits, `-`, `.`, `_`, and `~` stay, and every other
  UTF-8 byte becomes `%` and two uppercase hexadecimal digits. Authored
  `ENCODEURL` formulas are stored without a prefix.
- `BAHTTEXT(number)` reads the baht as Thai numerals (สิบ for ten, ยี่สิบ for
  twenty, เอ็ด for a one after a nonzero tens digit, หนึ่ง before the other
  place words, and ล้าน for each million), then บาท, then ถ้วน for a whole amount
  or the satang and สตางค์. Text that is not a number returns `#VALUE!`. Zero,
  negative amounts, amounts below one baht, more than two decimal places, and a
  final one after a zero tens digit (101, 1000001) report
  `calculation.unsupported_expression`.
- `CELL(info_type, reference)` calculates the info types defined by the
  workbook alone: `"address"` of the upper-left cell as `$A$1` text when the
  reference is on the formula's sheet, `"contents"` (the upper-left cell's
  value), and for a single cell `"row"`, `"col"`, and `"type"` (`"b"` for an
  empty cell, `"l"` for a text constant, and `"v"` otherwise). The other info
  types (formatting, width, protection, file name), an omitted reference,
  another sheet's address, a multi-cell `"row"`, `"col"`, or `"type"`, an empty
  cell's `"contents"`, a formula with a text result for `"type"`, and other
  info_type spellings report `calculation.unsupported_expression`. Because
  `CELL` depends on the referenced cells, a `CELL` formula that refers to its
  own cell is a circular reference.
- The three official names added in 0.1.26 are `RAND`, `RANDBETWEEN`, and
  `RANDARRAY`, with the edges measured in Excel. `RAND` returns a number in
  `[0, 1)`. `RANDBETWEEN(bottom, top)` returns `#NUM!` when `bottom` exceeds
  `top` or the span between them is too wide for a double; otherwise it returns
  an integer from `bottom` rounded up through `top`
  rounded down, both included, or `bottom` rounded up when no integer lies
  between them (`RANDBETWEEN(1.5,1.6)` is 2). `RANDARRAY([rows], [columns],
  [min], [max], [whole_number])` spills a `rows` by `columns` array (default 1
  by 1, truncated) of numbers from `min` up to `max` (default 0 and 1), or of
  the integers from `min` through `max` when `whole_number` is true; `min` may
  equal `max`. It returns `#VALUE!` for a negative dimension, `min` above `max`,
  or a fractional `min` or `max` with `whole_number`, `#CALC!` for a dimension
  that truncates to zero, and `#NUM!` when the span from `min` to `max` is too
  wide for a double. Authored `RANDARRAY` formulas are stored as
  `_xlfn.RANDARRAY`.
- `TEXT(value, format_text)` reads Excel number-format codes. Up to four
  `;`-separated sections format positive numbers, negative numbers (shown
  without their sign), zero, and text; one section formats every number and
  shows a minus sign, and an empty section shows nothing. `[<=100]`-style
  conditions on the first two sections select a section for a non-negative
  number; colors such as `[Red]` are accepted and not shown. Quoted text,
  `\x`, `[$symbol-lcid]` symbols, and characters other than codes are literal.
  Digit layouts use `0`, `#`, and `?` (a space when empty), `.`, `,` between
  integer placeholders for grouping, trailing `,` to divide by 1,000 each, `%`,
  `_x` as one space, literals between placeholders (`000-00-0000` fills digits
  from the right), `E+`/`E-` scientific notation (`##0.0E+0` keeps the
  exponent a multiple of three), and `# ?/?`-style fractions with the closest
  denominator of up to four digits. Digit rounding is half away from zero on
  the double, a minus sign appears only when a digit or `0` placeholder is
  shown, an integer `0` is kept unless decimals follow, the decimal point is
  omitted when no decimal digit is shown, and 2^53 or more rounded units is
  `#NUM!`. `General` shows the number as `&` does. Date sections read `yy`,
  `yyyy`, `e`, `m` through `mmmmm`, `d` through `dddd`, `h`, `hh`, minutes as
  `m`/`mm` after an hour or before a second, `s`, `ss`, `.0` to `.000`
  fractional seconds, `[h]`, `[m]`, `[s]`, `AM/PM`, and `A/P`, in the
  workbook's date system with serial 60 as 1900-02-29, rounded to the second
  or to the shown fraction of a second, with English month, weekday, and
  `AM`/`PM` names under the default locale profile. These stay
  `calculation.unsupported_expression`: `*` fills, fixed fraction
  denominators such as `# ?/8`, `@` in a number section, conditional sections
  for a negative number, lowercase `am/pm`, `aaa`, `b`, and `g` codes, system
  formats such as `[$-F800]`, names under a `[$-lcid]` other than `[$-409]`
  or under the Korean profile, negative date-time values, fractions that
  round to a whole number, and other year, day, hour, and second code
  lengths. A non-numeric text value is
  `#VALUE!`.
- `FIXED(number, [decimals], [no_commas])`, added in 0.1.27, and `DOLLAR(number,
  [decimals])` read numeric text as `VALUE` does, truncate `decimals` (default
  2; outside -308 through 127 is `#VALUE!`), and round a negative `decimals`
  to the left of the decimal point. `FIXED` rounds half away from zero first,
  so a negative number that rounds to zero has no sign, and groups thousands
  with `,` unless `no_commas` is true (`FIXED(-1234.567,-1,TRUE)` is `-1230`).
  `DOLLAR` shows `$#,##0.00` with the absolute value and wraps a negative
  number in parentheses. A `FIXED` result of 2^53 or more rounded units is
  `calculation.unsupported_expression`.
- The nine names `LENB`, `LEFTB`, `RIGHTB`, `MIDB`, `FINDB`, `SEARCHB`,
  `REPLACEB`, `ASC`, and `DBCS`, added in 0.1.27, follow the locale profile's
  double-byte rules. Under `Locale::EnUs` every character counts one byte, so
  the byte functions return what `LEN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `MID`, `FIND`,
  `SEARCH`, and `REPLACE` return, with the same argument coercion and
  `#VALUE!` boundaries. Under `Locale::KoKr` (code page 949) ASCII counts one
  byte and Hangul syllables, Hangul compatibility jamo, full-width ASCII forms
  (U+FF01 through U+FF5E), and the ideographic space count two; positions are
  one-based bytes, `FINDB`/`SEARCHB` return byte positions, and `SEARCHB`
  keeps `SEARCH` wildcards. `ASC` maps full-width ASCII forms to ASCII and the
  ideographic space to a space, leaving ASCII and Hangul syllables; `DBCS`
  maps printable ASCII to full-width forms and the space to the ideographic
  space, leaving double-byte characters. Other characters, a byte position or
  count that would split a double-byte character, and `ASC` and `DBCS` under
  `Locale::EnUs` are `calculation.unsupported_expression`. `JIS`, the Japanese
  name of `DBCS`, is not in the catalog.
- `AGGREGATE(function_num, options, ref1, ...)` and `AGGREGATE(function_num,
  options, array, k)`, added in 0.1.27, apply function 1 `AVERAGE`, 2 `COUNT`,
  3 `COUNTA`, 4 `MAX`, 5 `MIN`, 6 `PRODUCT`, 7 `STDEV.S`, 8 `STDEV.P`, 9 `SUM`,
  10 `VAR.S`, 11 `VAR.P` (as `SUBTOTAL` does), 12 `MEDIAN`, 13 `MODE.SNGL`, 14
  `LARGE`, 15 `SMALL`, 16 `PERCENTILE.INC`, 17 `QUARTILE.INC`, 18
  `PERCENTILE.EXC`, or 19 `QUARTILE.EXC`. Options 0 to 3 skip cells whose
  formula calls `SUBTOTAL` or `AGGREGATE`, odd options skip rows
  `Sheet::hidden_rows` lists, and 2, 3, 6, and 7 skip error values; an
  omitted option is 0. Functions 1 to 13 take only references (a constant
  array is `#VALUE!`); 14 to 19 take one reference or calculated array and a
  required `k`, and a calculated array keeps its hidden rows and nested
  totals. 3-D references and a function or option outside 1-19 or 0-7 are
  `#VALUE!`. An option that keeps hidden rows (0, 2, 4, 6) over a hidden row
  inside a sheet or table autoFilter with a filter condition is
  `calculation.unsupported_expression`, because whether Excel then keeps the
  rows the filter hides has not been measured. Authored formulas are stored
  as `_xlfn.AGGREGATE`.
- The 22 official names added in 0.1.22 are `PERCENTILE.EXC`, `QUARTILE.EXC`, `PERCENTRANK.EXC`, `TRIMMEAN`,
  `STDEVA`, `STDEVPA`, `VARA`, `VARPA`, `STEYX`, `FISHER`, `FISHERINV`, `PROB`,
  `CHISQ.DIST`, `CHISQ.DIST.RT`, `CHIDIST`, `WEIBULL.DIST`, `WEIBULL`,
  `CONFIDENCE.NORM`, `CONFIDENCE`, `CONFIDENCE.T`, `IMLOG10`, and `IMLOG2`.
  `CHIDIST`, `WEIBULL`, and `CONFIDENCE` are legacy aliases. Right tails such as
  `CHISQ.DIST.RT` are computed directly rather than as one minus the CDF.
- The sixteen official names added in 0.1.20 are `CODE`, `NUMBERVALUE`, `DDB`,
  `XNPV`, `MDETERM`, `RANK.AVG`, `FORECAST.LINEAR`, `FORECAST`, `NORM.INV`,
  `NORM.S.INV`, `NORMINV`, `NORMSINV`, `LOGNORM.DIST`, `LOGNORM.INV`,
  `LOGNORMDIST`, and `LOGINV`. All return scalars. Legacy aliases preserve the
  modern signatures except `LOGNORMDIST(x, mean, standard_dev)`, which always
  returns the CDF and has no cumulative argument.
- `CODE` returns the first character's deterministic Windows-1252 code, using
  the same mapping as `CHAR`; empty or unmappable text returns `#VALUE!`.
  `NUMBERVALUE(text, [decimal_separator], [group_separator])` uses `.` and `,`
  when a separator is absent or missing. Explicit separators use their first
  character and must be nonempty and different. ASCII space/tab/CR/LF are
  ignored unless chosen as a separator; trailing percent signs scale by 100
  each. Empty/whitespace-only text yields zero, and parentheses denote a
  negative number. Malformed numbers return `#VALUE!`; no host locale is read.
- `RANK.AVG` averages the positions of equal numeric values; `RANK`/`RANK.EQ`
  return the first such position. They count values in one pass without sorting.
  `FORECAST.LINEAR`/`FORECAST` reuse paired numeric regression moments and
  evaluate the centered line at `x`; unequal lengths return `#N/A`, and absent
  usable pairs or constant known-x values return `#DIV/0!`.
- `DDB(cost, salvage, life, period, [factor])` defaults an absent factor to 2,
  computes declining book value directly, and caps depreciation at the salvage
  floor. `XNPV(rate, values, dates)` discounts actual elapsed days over 365,
  shares XIRR's date/value validation, and permits cash flows of only one sign.
  `MDETERM` requires a square numeric array, propagates input errors, and returns
  zero for a singular matrix. Its LU elimination observes work/workspace limits.
  See `docs/NUMERICS.md` for numerical and boundary policies.
- The 19 official names added in 0.1.14 are `CONVERT`, `BESSELI`, `BESSELJ`,
  `BESSELK`, `BESSELY`, `COMPLEX`, `IMABS`, `IMAGINARY`, `IMARGUMENT`,
  `IMCONJUGATE`, `IMREAL`, `IMDIV`, `IMPOWER`, `IMPRODUCT`, `IMSUB`, `IMSUM`,
  `IMEXP`, `IMLN`, and `IMSQRT`. None returns an array.
- The 26 official fixed-income names added on top of 0.1.14 are `ACCRINT`,
  `ACCRINTM`, `COUPDAYBS`, `COUPDAYS`, `COUPDAYSNC`, `COUPNCD`, `COUPNUM`,
  `COUPPCD`, `DISC`, `DURATION`, `INTRATE`, `MDURATION`, `ODDFPRICE`,
  `ODDFYIELD`, `ODDLPRICE`, `ODDLYIELD`, `PRICE`, `PRICEDISC`, `PRICEMAT`,
  `RECEIVED`, `TBILLEQ`, `TBILLPRICE`, `TBILLYIELD`, `YIELD`, `YIELDDISC`,
  and `YIELDMAT`. None returns an array.
- The four 0.1.16 official names are `DATEVALUE`, `TIMEVALUE`,
  `NETWORKDAYS.INTL`, and `WORKDAY.INTL`. `XLOOKUP` is now implemented and is
  marked `.returns_array()`. It accepts a one-dimensional lookup vector and a
  matching-axis return range; the array result is the matching row (vertical
  lookup) or column (horizontal lookup). It supports exact, next-smaller,
  next-larger, and linear wildcard matching, plus forward, reverse, ascending
  binary, and descending binary search. Binary search assumes correctly sorted
  caller input and wildcard mode rejects binary search. `if_not_found` is lazy
  and is evaluated only for no-match.
- `DATEVALUE` accepts space/tab-trimmed ASCII `YYYY-MM-DD`; `TIMEVALUE` accepts
  the same trimming with ASCII `HH:MM`, optional seconds, and one-to-nine
  fractional-second digits.
  Both reject locale-dependent input. `DATEVALUE` validates Gregorian fields
  and maps `1900-02-29` to serial 60 only in the Excel 1900 system.
  `NETWORKDAYS.INTL` and `WORKDAY.INTL` support numeric weekend codes 1..7 and
  11..17 or a seven-bit Monday-first mask, deduplicate numeric holidays, and
  charge the iteration budget while observing cancellation.
- Fixed-income day counts cover US 30/360, Actual/Actual, Actual/360,
  Actual/365, and European 30/360; coupon schedules walk backward from
  maturity and preserve month-end policy. `YIELD(N>1)` and `ODDFYIELD` share
  a safeguarded Newton/bracket root solver bounded to 100 evaluations in
  Excel-compatible mode, charging the calculation budget and observing
  cancellation per evaluation.
- `CONVERT` uses a case-sensitive typed unit registry with explicit decimal and
  binary prefix policies. Complex functions share one finite internal value,
  parser, suffix policy, canonical text formatter, and scaled arithmetic.
  Bessel J/Y and I/K use separate first-party numerical families; their
  iterative work consumes the calculation budget and observes cancellation.
- All four families share one first-party special-function foundation: a
  Lanczos `ln_gamma`, regularized incomplete gamma and beta kernels, and a
  safeguarded inverse solver. A family's cumulative and quantile forms are
  evaluated through the same tail kernel; the density forms are built on the
  same primitives.
- The inverse solver brackets and then refines with alternating bisection and
  secant steps, and charges the calculation budget for every step. A search
  that cannot converge returns `#N/A` from `GAMMA.INV` and `BETA.INV`, which is
  the error Microsoft documents; it never returns an unconverged number.
- `BINOM.INV` and `CRITBINOM` bisect over the integer support instead, and
  verify `CDF(k-1) < alpha <= CDF(k)` against regularized incomplete-beta CDF
  evaluations before returning. Full-support and degenerate CDFs resolve exactly
  without enumerating the support; paths that require exact integer indexing
  reject support indices above `2^53` instead of using a lossy conversion.
  Binomial and negative-binomial mass complements use `ln1p(-p)` so tiny
  probabilities survive exponentiation over large counts.
- `HYPGEOM.DIST` and `HYPGEOMDIST` evaluate sample sizes through 10,000 as a
  falling-factorial product that never differences two large `lnGamma` values,
  which is what keeps very large populations accurate.
- `scan_function_usage(&WorkbookSnapshot) -> FunctionUsageReport` and
  `scan_function_usage_with_options(&WorkbookSnapshot, CalculationOptions)`
  count normalized function calls without calculating the workbook.
- `FunctionUsageEntry` exposes `.name()`, `.support()`, `.call_count()`,
  `.formula_count()`, and up to eight deterministic `.sample_cells()`.
  `FunctionUsageReport` also records parsed and unparsed formula counts.
- Demand is static, including repeated defined-name references, rather than a runtime
  execution counter. Completed acyclic name summaries are reused within one scan;
  scope and cycle-cut semantics remain intact. Counts saturate at `u64::MAX`:
  values below `18446744073709551615` are exact; that maximum means at least that many.
