- Function usage report schema version 2 preserves `call_count` as a decimal string
  in interop JSON and MCP. Rust DTOs retain `u64`, Python exposes `int`, and Node's
  public `callCount` is `bigint`. Other reports keep their existing schema versions.
  Node consumers must use bigint arithmetic and explicitly convert counts with
  `.toString()` when serializing to JSON; converting through `Number` loses precision.
- `FunctionSupport`: `Supported | Unsupported`; it is independent from
  whether a particular call later produces an Excel error value.

### Calculation

- `CalculationTarget::cell(CalculationCellId)` requests one cell;
  `CalculationTarget::new(SheetId, CellRange)` requests an inclusive rectangle.
  `TargetCalculationLimits::new(max_targets, max_result_cells, max_evaluated_cells)`
  requires nonzero `usize` values; defaults are 1024, 10000, and 100000.
- `calculate_targets(&WorkbookSnapshot, &[CalculationTarget], CalculationOptions,
  TargetCalculationLimits, CancellationToken) -> Result<TargetCalculationResult, TargetCalculationError>`
  needs no previous calculation. It parses/evaluates the selected formulas and required precedents,
  inspecting workbook layout metadata without globally parsing formula text. Overlap is deduplicated.
  Literals and empty cells return their typed value or Blank. Unrelated cycles/unsupported formulas
  are outside this request. Static names, sheets, table references and supported 3D references reuse
  the full evaluator; dynamic references can discover additional precedents during evaluation.
- `TargetCalculationResult` is separate from `CalculationSnapshot`. `.cells()` contains only
  requested cells, ordered by sheet ID, row, column. `.cell(id)`, `.source_revision()`,
  `.source_fingerprint()`, `.provenance()`, `.options()`, `.limits()`, `.evaluated_count()`,
  `.parsed_formula_count()`, and `.reused_count()` expose scope and provenance. Evaluated count
  includes dynamic-reference retries and a scoped second pass for newly discovered spills.
  Results never enable save, replace the complete cache, clear dirty formulas, advance deltas,
  or invalidate retained previews. Resource failures cannot publish incomplete requested output.
- `WorkbookCalculationSession::prepare_target_calculation(targets, options, limits, token)`
  captures an owned `PreparedTargetCalculation`; `.run()` returns `CompletedTargetCalculation`.
  `session.finish_target_calculation(completed)` validates cancellation and source state without
  installing anything. `session.calculate_targets(...)` is the synchronous convenience method.
  A complete calculation is reused only for the same source identity/revision and calculation
  options (including formula limits). Partial results are not retained as a new cache.
- Known legacy-array and dynamic-spill followers evaluate their complete anchor, retaining the
  existing collision and array limits. An undeclared spill follower with no known owner cannot
  discover an arbitrary anchor elsewhere: include the anchor in the targets, or use a current
  complete calculation. Saved formula results never supply current values.
  Undeclared spills outside the dependency scope are not discovered; use declared spill ranges
  or full calculation when independently anchored spills may overlap.
- Python: `workbook.calculate_targets([{"sheet": "Sheet1", "start": "B1", "end": "B10"}],
  today_serial=..., now_serial=..., random_seed=..., locale_profile=...,
  arithmetic_semantics=...,
  financial_solver_semantics=...,
  limits={"max_result_cells": 100}) -> TargetCalculationResult`; omit `end` for one cell.
  Node: `await workbook.calculateTargets([{sheet: "Sheet1", start: "B1", end: "B10"}],
  {limits: {maxResultCells: 100}}) -> TargetCalculationResult`. Node uses camel case and a bigint
  semanticRevision; Python uses snake case and an int. Both run native evaluation off-lock;
  Python releases the GIL and Node uses a worker. Cancellation, supersession and close use the
  existing active-calculation lifecycle.
- MCP `workbook_calculate_targets` takes `session_id`, `targets`, optional `options` and `limits`,
  with snake-case interop fields. The server caps limits at the defaults above and rejects a
  response that cannot fit `--max-response-bytes` in full. There is no partial-result paging
  registry. Responses include `scope: "targets"`, `semantic_revision`, `source_fingerprint`,
  `input_sha256`, `calculator_provider`, `calculation_options`, `limits`, `cells`, and all three
  work counts. Each cell contains `cell` (sheet ID/name/address) and `result` (value or issue).
- `TargetCalculationErrorCode::as_str()` returns `calculation.target.empty_targets`,
  `.sheet_not_found`, `.invalid_limits`, `.target_limit_exceeded`, `.evaluation_limit_exceeded`,
  `.cancelled`, or `.stale_result` under the same `calculation.target` prefix. Bindings also use
  existing address/sheet validation and active-request cancellation codes.
  `TargetCalculationError::requested_cell_count() -> Option<u64>` returns the requested cells
  counted when the result-cell limit stopped a request, a lower bound on the distinct cells it
  names: a target larger than the limit reports its own cell count, and otherwise counting stops
  at the first distinct cell past the limit. A request stopped by the target-count limit reports
  `None`.
  `.evaluated_count() -> Option<usize>` returns the evaluations performed before the work limit
  stopped a request, counted like `TargetCalculationResult::evaluated_count()`.

- `calculate_workbook(&WorkbookSnapshot, CalculationOptions) -> CalculationSnapshot` —
  stateless full recalculation and the correctness oracle; never mutates the
  source snapshot.
- `CalculationOptions::default().with_today_serial(FiniteNumber).with_now_serial(FiniteNumber).with_random_seed(u32).with_limits(CalculationLimits).with_arithmetic_semantics(ArithmeticSemantics).with_financial_solver_semantics(FinancialSolverSemantics)` —
  `TODAY()` and `NOW()` never read the host clock, and `RAND()`,
  `RANDBETWEEN()`, and `RANDARRAY()` never read host randomness. Omitting the
  corresponding serial or seed makes that formula report
  `VolatileInputMissing`; `.random_seed() -> Option<u32>` returns the seed.
  A draw is keyed by the seed, the formula cell's stable sheet ID and
  address, the call's position in the formula (followed through defined-name
  references and LAMBDA calls), the `MAKEARRAY`/`MAP`/`BYROW`/`BYCOL`/`SCAN`/
  `REDUCE` iteration or `GROUPBY`/`PIVOTBY` group that reached it, the
  computed database-criteria record, and the `RANDARRAY` element. It never
  depends on calculation order: wherever full calculation produces a value,
  targeted, incremental, and preview calculation produce the same one, and
  edits to unrelated cells leave a draw unchanged; supply a new seed for a new
  draw. A dynamic reference whose position is drawn inside a defined name used
  more than once or inside a `LAMBDA` body can still be reported as
  unsupported by full calculation, as one driven by a `LAMBDA` parameter is.
  `=RAND()-RAND()` uses two positions and is not zero, while a `LET` binding
  draws once. The generator is a small SplitMix64-style counter mixer, not a
  cryptographically secure source.
- `CalculationOptions::with_locale_profile(LocaleProfile)` selects built-in
  locale conventions; CellRune never reads the host locale.
  `LocaleProfile::new(Locale)` follows one locale for the regional format and
  for generated labels, and `.with_display_language(Locale)` sets the labels
  apart; `.locale()` and `.display_language()` read them back. `Locale` is
  `#[non_exhaustive]` with `EnUs` (the default, which keeps every earlier
  result) and `KoKr`; both use `.` and `,` as decimal and thousands
  separators. The regional format decides the `DOLLAR` currency symbol (`$`
  or `₩`) and the decimals it shows when the formula omits them (2 or none;
  negative amounts are parenthesized in both), and the names `TEXT` shows:
  English for `EnUs`, while Korean month, weekday, and `AM`/`PM` names are
  `calculation.unsupported_expression` until measured (a `[$-409]` section
  still shows English names), and the double-byte rules of `LENB`, `LEFTB`,
  `RIGHTB`, `MIDB`, `FINDB`, `SEARCHB`, `REPLACEB`, `ASC`, and `DBCS`. The
  display language decides the `GROUPBY` and
  `PIVOTBY` total label: `Total` or `합계`, and `Grand Total` over several
  levels in English, which is unsupported in Korean. Changing the profile is
  a calculation-options change, so a session recalculates fully.
- `format_display_text(&CellValue, format_code: &str, DateSystem, LocaleProfile)
  -> Result<String, DisplayFormatError>` returns the text a cell shows. Numbers
  go through the `TEXT` engine with the profile's names; text goes through the
  code's text section (the fourth section, or a lone section holding `@`) and
  is otherwise unchanged; logical and error values show `TRUE`, `FALSE`, or the
  error; a blank shows nothing. `General` is not shortened to a column width,
  and a `*` fill is unsupported because the width is not an input.
  `DisplayFormatError::Unsupported` (`.code()` `display_format.unsupported`)
  covers every construct `TEXT` leaves unsupported and numbers past 2^53
  rounded units. Interop `format_display_text(DisplayFormatRequestDto { value,
  format_code, date_system, locale_profile }) -> DisplayFormatResultDto { text }`
  takes a `WritableCellValueDto` and `DateSystemDto` (`"excel_1900"`, the
  default, or `"excel_1904"`); Python `format_display_text(value, format_code,
  *, date_system=..., locale_profile=...) -> str` and Node.js
  `formatDisplayText(value, formatCode, { dateSystem, localeProfile }) -> string`
  take the `{kind, value}` cell values `read_range` returns, and MCP has the
  sessionless `format_display_text` tool. A request bindings cannot read is
  `interop.display_format.request_invalid`.
- **Two numeric-compatibility axes, both defaulting to Excel's behavior rather
  than to what 0.1.2 did.** `ArithmeticSemantics`: `ExcelNearZero` (default)
  applies Excel's narrow correction only when the exact decimal/rational trace
  is zero and the binary residue is within `1e-15` of the cancelling operands'
  relative scale. Thus `=0.1+0.2-0.3` is `0`, while
  `=100.1-100-0.1` retains `-5.689893001203927e-15`, matching the committed
  Excel saved cache. `Ieee754` leaves every residue. The correction reaches
  the operator path, the array path, and the running totals behind `SUM`,
  `AVERAGE`, `SUMIF(S)`, `AVERAGEIF(S)`, `SUBTOTAL`, `SUMPRODUCT`, and `NPV`,
  so those cannot disagree with each other.
  `FinancialSolverSemantics`: `ExcelIterationBudget` (default) applies
  Microsoft's per-function budget — 20 iterations/`1e-7` for `IRR` and `RATE`,
  100/`1e-8` for `XIRR` — so inputs Excel abandons yield `#NUM!` here too;
  `ExtendedSearch` searches longer, as 0.1.2 did. **Upgrading from 0.1.2
  changes calculated numbers unless you select `ArithmeticSemantics::Ieee754`
  and `FinancialSolverSemantics::ExtendedSearch`.** Both axes are also carried
  by the interop DTO and the Python, Node.js, and MCP boundaries.
  The random seed is carried the same way: `CalculationOptionsDto.random_seed`
  and the transaction report's `calculation_options.random_seed`, Python
  `random_seed=` on `calculate`, `recalculate`, `calculate_targets`, and
  `preview_changes`, Node.js `randomSeed` on `calculate`, `recalculate`,
  `calculateTargets`, and `previewChanges`, and MCP `random_seed` on
  `workbook_recalculate`, `workbook_calculate_targets` `options`, and
  `workbook_preview_changes`. A seed must be an integer from 0 through
  4294967295: Python rejects other values with `interop.value.number_invalid`,
  Node.js with `interop.input.invalid`, and the JSON targeted and MCP payloads
  as invalid payloads.
  The locale profile is carried the same way: `CalculationOptionsDto.locale_profile`
  is an optional `LocaleProfileDto { locale, display_language }` of `LocaleDto`
  tags `"en-US"` or `"ko-KR"` (an omitted display language follows `locale`),
  and the transaction report's `calculation_options.locale_profile` records
  the profile in effect with the display language resolved. Python
  `locale_profile={"locale": "ko-KR", "display_language": "en-US"}` and
  Node.js `localeProfile: { locale: "ko-KR", displayLanguage: "en-US" }` work
  on `calculate`, `recalculate`, targeted calculation, and previews, and MCP
  `locale_profile` on `workbook_recalculate`, `workbook_calculate_targets`
  `options`, and `workbook_preview_changes`. An unknown tag or key is
  `interop.calculation.locale_profile_invalid` from Python and from Node.js
  `calculate` and `recalculate`, Node.js rejects a value that is not an object
  of strings with `interop.input.invalid`, and JSON targeted, Node.js preview,
  and MCP payloads fail as invalid payloads.
  `docs/NUMERICS.md` records the policies and their oracles.
- `CalculationLimits::default()` + 12 `.with_max_*(u64) -> Result<Self, CalculationOptionsError>`
  budgets: formula tokens, source bytes, AST nodes, AST nesting depth,
  dependency edges, reference areas, array cells, calculated text bytes,
  data-dependent function iterations, LET bindings, active LAMBDA depth, and
  cumulative LAMBDA/MAP invocations. A `ResourceLimitExceeded` issue names the
  exceeded budget through `CalculationIssue::limit() ->
  Option<CalculationLimitKind>`, a non-exhaustive enum with one variant per
  budget; its `.detail()` remains the `max_*` limit name.
- `LAMBDA` is a first-class scoped value. Literal, immediate, `LET`-bound,
  workbook-defined, and sheet-local callables share one evaluator with lexical
  capture and caller isolation. `MAP`, `BYROW`, `BYCOL`, `REDUCE`, `SCAN`,
  `MAKEARRAY`, and `ISOMITTED` consume the same typed callable representation;
  final callable results are `#CALC!`, while attempts to use a callable as a
  scalar operand are `#VALUE!`.
- `CalculationSnapshot`: `.cell(CalculationCellId) -> Option<&CalculationCellResult>`,
  `.cells()`, `.materialized_cell(CalculationCellId)`,
  `.materialized_cells()`, `.len()`, `.is_empty()`, `.options()`,
  `.provenance()`.
- `MaterializedCalculationCell` carries `.origin()` and `.result()`.
  `MaterializedResultOrigin` distinguishes a direct formula cell, a cell in
  a legacy-array region, and a cell in a dynamic-spill region; array origins
  carry their anchor and complete result range.
- `CalculationCellId::new(SheetId, CellAddress)`.
- `CalculationCellResult`: `Value(CellValue) | Unavailable(CalculationIssue)`.
- `INDEX(reference, 0, column)` returns the selected complete column,
  `INDEX(reference, row, 0)` returns the selected complete row, and zero for
  both indexes returns the complete reference. Scalar formulas apply legacy
  implicit intersection; array contexts materialize the selected rectangle.
- Unary and binary array operators containing whole-column references resolve
  one common row extent from the greatest populated row among the columns
  those operands reference, with a one-row minimum on an otherwise empty
  sheet. Cells in other columns of the same sheet do not widen it, so the
  value depends only on the cells the expression's dependency rectangles
  cover and a full and an incremental recalculation agree. Unpopulated cells
  in that extent are `Blank`; directly resolved source arrays and operator
  outputs are charged cumulatively to `max_array_cells`. Function calls retain
  function-defined argument boundaries: each array argument has an
  independent bounded evaluation context, and a function return does not
  establish a whole-column operator extent by itself. If another direct
  whole-column operand establishes an enclosing context, the returned array
  is charged to that context before the operator consumes it.
- Direct 3-D references are supported for `SUM`, `AVERAGE`, `AVERAGEA`,
  `COUNT`, `COUNTA`, `MAX`, `MAXA`, `MIN`, `MINA`, `PRODUCT`, `STDEV.P`,
  `STDEV.S`, `VAR.P`, and `VAR.S`, including catalogued legacy aliases.
  Workbook tab order defines the inclusive span, including hidden sheets;
  reversing the written endpoints does not change the participating sheets.
  Direct 3-D arguments to `INDEX` and `VLOOKUP` produce `#VALUE!`, and
  `OFFSET` produces `#REF!`. Other direct consumers report
  `UnsupportedSheetRange`. Bare 3-D references and 3-D references composed
  through array operators produce `#VALUE!`; an enclosing aggregate does not
  widen that nested context. The scanner and evaluator use the same policy.
  Incremental dependency state stores each 3-D input as one compact
  rectangle span rather than one rectangle per sheet, so compiled size grows
  with the number of references, not with the number of sheets spanned. The
  span is expanded only while building graph edges. A multi-cell range
  becomes shared areas of aligned row or column blocks, so formulas over
  overlapping ranges, such as running totals `SUM($B$2:Bn)`, reuse them. A
  formula counts toward `max_dependency_edges` one edge per cell or area it
  waits for and one per member of each area it builds, but never more than
  the distinct formula cells and array anchors its references cover.
- Structured table references (`Table1[Amount]`, `[@Amount]`, item selectors,
  column spans, nested/escaped column spellings, a selector list's column
  name without brackets, as in xlsxwriter's `[[#This Row],Qty]`, and a
  table-qualified column name with `_`, `\ ! ( ) % ? ; ~`, a backtick, or
  `. - @ & =`, which Excel brackets only in a selector list, as in
  `Orders[unit_price]`) are typed and resolved against stable table/column
  identities. Empty data or totals bands remain a valid empty reference, while
  `#This Row` uses the formula's actual table row. Dependencies retain table
  identity and topology, so table rename or resize forces a safe graph rebuild
  rather than reusing stale geometry.
- Reference union, intersection, and range operators preserve ordered
  multi-area identity. `AREAS` is in the official catalog; consumers that
  require one rectangle fail with the documented Excel error rather than
  silently flattening a multi-area value.
- Spill postfix references such as `A1#` and the OOXML storage form
  `_xlfn.ANCHORARRAY(A1)` share one typed node. Evaluation resolves the
  current spill registry, schedules the producer anchor first, rejects
  non-anchors, propagates blocked spills, and removes stale spill children
  when a shape changes.
- External-workbook references and sheet-qualified defined names are typed by
  the parser. External workbook calculation remains unsupported and never
  opens or follows the referenced package.

### Diagnostics and provenance

- `DiagnosticSeverity`: `Info | Warning | Error`.
- `SourceLocation::source`, `::sheet`, and `::cell` construct source-linked
  locations; `.with_byte_offset(...)` adds a zero-based byte offset.
- `Provenance` pairs a `ProviderIdentity` with an optional `InputHash`.
- `OutputHash` is a distinct SHA-256 newtype for exact verified output archive
  bytes. `WriteReport::output_hash()` returns it only on a successful write;
  never use it as an input identity.
- `WriteProvenance` records the input hash, semantic and presentation
  revisions, calculator identity, and deterministic calculation options used
  by a completed write.

## Error taxonomy — pick the right one, never mix

| Type | Means | Result exists? | Machine check |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ValidationError` | Caller-supplied address/name/number/model value violates an invariant | No object is produced | `.code(): ValidationErrorCode`; match on the non-exhaustive enum only when structured fields are needed |
| `ReadOptionsError` | A `ReadLimits` budget was invalid (zero) | Fails before reading starts | Match on the enum variant |
| `CalculationOptionsError` | A `CalculationLimits` budget was invalid (zero) | Fails before calculation starts | Match on the enum variant |
| `DefinedNameAnalysisOptionsError` | A defined-name chain or scan budget was invalid (zero) | Fails before inspection starts | Match the concrete error type |
| `DefinedNameAnalysisError` | Defined-name inspection saw an unknown current sheet, exhausted a budget, or was cancelled | No semantic inspection result is produced | `.kind()`, optional `.limit()`, and `.detail()` |
| `XlsxReadError` | No trustworthy `WorkbookSnapshot` could be produced at all | No snapshot | `.code(): XlsxErrorCode`, `.source_id()`, `.detail()`, optional `.observed()` and `.phonetic_run_limit()` |
| `WriteOptionsError` | A `WriteLimits` budget was invalid (zero) | Fails before writing starts | Match on the enum variant |
| `XlsxWriteError` | The source/calculation binding, package plan, write budget, destination, or completed output was invalid | No successful output artifact | `.code(): XlsxWriteErrorCode`, `.source_id()`, `.detail()`, and for `IncompleteCalculation` `.unavailable_formulas()` (first 64) |
| `ApplyChangesError` | An atomic session edit failed either session-state or workbook validation | No edit is committed | Match `Session` or `Validation` |
| `SessionError` | Revision, incremental-safety, cancellation, cursor, or session resource rules rejected an operation | Session remains valid; installation is rejected when applicable | `.code(): SessionErrorCode`, `.detail()` |
| `Diagnostic` | Read succeeded, but a compatibility caveat exists (e.g. external link, macro) | Snapshot exists, on `.diagnostics()` | `.code(): DiagnosticCode`, `.severity()`, `.location()` |
| `CalculationIssue` | One specific formula could not be calculated | Independent formulas can still produce results; dependents may report `BlockedByUpstream` | `.code(): CalculationIssueCode`, `.detail()`, optional `.limit()` |
| `CellValue::Error(ExcelError)` | An actual spreadsheet error value (`#DIV/0!`, `#REF!`, ...) | This *is* the cell's value | `.as_str()` on the `ExcelError` |

An unsupported engine capability is never converted into an `ExcelError` and
can never be hidden by a spreadsheet-side `IFERROR`/`IFNA` — it always
surfaces as a `CalculationIssue`, which is a Rust-level fact about the
engine, not a spreadsheet-level fact about the data.

## Scope / non-goals

CellRune supports ordinary Transitional SpreadsheetML workbooks and a scoped
set of Excel formula syntax and functions. Unsupported formulas appear as
structured per-cell calculation issues while independent formulas continue to
calculate. Out of scope for the current version:

- Browser, frontend/UI, WebAssembly, hosted-service, and remote-MCP transports.
- `.xls`, `.xlsb`, and `.ods`.
- Macro, add-in, external-workbook, query, or data-connection execution.
- 3-D references outside the audited direct-consumer policy described under
  Calculation, and data-table calculation.
- Iterative calculation and automatic host-time or random inputs (`TODAY()`,
  `NOW()`, `RAND()`, `RANDBETWEEN()`, and `RANDARRAY()` are supported only
  through explicit `CalculationOptions` inputs).

## Development verification

- `cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked` runs the standard Rust test
  suite.
- `conformance/README.md` documents the Excel-saved and Apache POI fixture
  layout, focused audit command, classifications, maintenance policy, and
  optional local corpus tests.

## Runnable examples

The repository path is `crates/cellrune/examples/`; the published crate
package path is `examples/`. From the repository root use
`cargo run -p cellrune --example <name> -- [arguments]`. From an extracted
crate package use `cargo run --example <name> -- [arguments]`.

- `read_only_inspection.rs` — read a workbook and inspect cells/diagnostics
  without ever calling `calculate_workbook`.
- `capability_scan_only.rs` — build an optional static formula-capability
  inventory and inspect `FormulaCapability`.
- `handle_read_error.rs` — match on `XlsxErrorCode` for a deliberately
  invalid input; the stable-code contract, concretely.
- `compare_saved_vs_calculated.rs` — reads a formula's `SavedResult` and a
  fresh `calculate_workbook` result side by side, demonstrating that neither
  operation touches the other.
- `read_and_calculate.rs` — the full pipeline against a real file (takes a
  path argument); also prints per-issue diagnostics for a whole workbook.
- `create_and_write.rs` — creates, calculates, and writes a canonical workbook
  (optional destination path argument).
- `recalculate_and_save.rs` — opens an XLSX/XLSM package, recalculates it, and
  performs verified Save As (input and output path arguments).
- `dynamic_array_write.rs` — authors, calculates, and writes a canonical
  `FILTER` spill (optional destination path argument).
- `inspect_phonetic_workbook.rs` — prints frozen-pane metadata and, for each
  annotated cell, the byte range and base slice each run covers; shows the
  `phonetic_cell_entries` → workbook base text → `resolved_runs` join a
  consumer needs (input path argument).
- `write_phonetic_workbook.rs` — authors annotated text and a frozen pane
  (output path argument).
- `select_calculation_modes.rs` — calculates the same formulas under the
  default Excel-compatible policies and under the 0.1.2 opt-ins, so the numbers
  `ArithmeticSemantics` and `FinancialSolverSemantics` change are visible side
  by side (no arguments).
